title: Beyond RSV: why the bronchiolitis burden in infants will not simply disappear.
abstract: Nirsevimab and maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination are delivering real-world important reductions in RSV-bronchiolitis hospitalisations, a landmark achievement in paediatric preventive medicine. We argue, however, that these successes should not be mistaken for the resolution of severe bronchiolitis as a clinical and public health problem. First, RSV's epidemiological dominance may partly reflect its transmission efficiency rather than a unique pathogenic superiority: rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus, and bocavirus already cause substantial disease, and genetic variants in CDHR3, GSDMB, and innate immune genes indicate that host susceptibility, not pathogen identity, is a key driver of severity. Second, although current evidence does not support viral replacement, the possibility that other respiratory viruses could expand into the ecological niche vacated by suppressed RSV transmission warrants close monitoring, alongside the theoretical, fitness-limited risk of nirsevimab-resistant RSV escape variants. Third, important gaps remain in long-term virological surveillance, cost-effectiveness evaluation, and equitable global access, particularly for the low- and middle-income countries that bear over 97% of RSV-attributable mortality. Conclusion: We contend that bronchiolitis should be understood as a syndrome reflecting the infant airway's stereotyped response to viral injury, rather than a disease defined by a single pathogen. Sustained broad-spectrum surveillance, transparent cost-effectiveness monitoring, and continued investment in a pan-respiratory mucosal vaccine pipeline are needed to ensure that early success against RSV translates into a durable reduction of the overall infant bronchiolitis burden. What is Known: • Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination are producing substantial real-world reductions in RSV-bronchiolitis hospitalisations, a major success in paediatric preventive medicine. What is New: • We argue that the control of RSV does not equate to the control of severe infant bronchiolitis. Other respiratory viruses-rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus and bocavirus-already cause substantial disease and could expand into the ecological niche left by suppressed RSV transmission, while host genetic susceptibility, not pathogen identity, remains a key driver of severity. We call for sustained broad spectrum viral surveillance to ensure that success against RSV translates into a durable reduction of the overall bronchiolitis burden, rather than its replacement by other pathogens.

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

analysis.main_results: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001).

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted preventative programs for Indigenous children, those born prematurely and children with cardiac disease, as well as guide the implementation of RSV immunisation programs in Australia.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, involving 4414 children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% were admitted to ICU.
analysis_en.methods: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission were identified using multivariate logistic regression.
analysis_en.main_results: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted preventative programs for Indigenous children, those born prematurely and children with cardiac disease, as well as guide the implementation of RSV immunisation programs in Australia.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted before the implementation of government-funded immunisation programs, which may limit its generalisability. The evidence is strong, with a high confidence assessment based on the comprehensive data collection and statistical analysis.

title_zh: 2019-2023 年悉尼儿童医院网络收治的幼儿的增强型 呼吸道合胞病毒 监测。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: Perceived barriers to respiratory syncytial virus vaccination and vaccination coverage among pregnant women: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: Argentina introduced maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in 2024 to prevent severe respiratory infections in infants. To ensure satisfactory vaccination rates, it is important to identify barriers to its implementation. To identify barriers to RSV vaccination among pregnant women. We estimated RSV vaccination coverage and the potential association between coverage and barriers. Population and methods. A cross-sectional study based on a survey of mothers who were eligible to receive the RSV vaccine. We developed and validated a tool to identify structural, informational, emotional, and social barriers. We used logistic regression for univariate and multivariate analyses. We surveyed 216 mothers. RSV vaccine coverage was 43.7%. In the univariate analysis, fewer than 5 prenatal visits and not receiving clear information were associated with lower vaccination rates. In the multivariate analysis, knowledge of the RSV vaccine was the only factor independently associated with vaccination coverage (adjusted OR: 3.4; 95% CI: 1.9-6.2; p <0.001). RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women was lower than that for other vaccines recommended during pregnancy. We identified limited vaccine availability and limited knowledge about the vaccine as factors associated with non-vaccination. Strengthening information and recommendations during prenatal care could help improve vaccination coverage. This study provides a validated tool for assessing barriers to vaccination among pregnant women.

title_zh: 孕妇 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 和 疫苗接种 覆盖的感知障碍:一项横断面研究。
source_body_en: Argentina introduced maternal vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in 2024 to prevent severe respiratory infections in infants. To ensure satisfactory vaccination rates, it is important to identify barriers to its implementation. To identify barriers to RSV vaccination among pregnant women. We estimated RSV vaccination coverage and the potential association between coverage and barriers. Population and methods. A cross-sectional study based on a survey of mothers who were eligible to receive the RSV vaccine. We developed and validated a tool to identify structural, informational, emotional, and social barriers. We used logistic regression for univariate and multivariate analyses. We surveyed 216 mothers. RSV vaccine coverage was 43.7%. In the univariate analysis, fewer than 5 prenatal visits and not receiving clear information were associated with lower vaccination rates. In the multivariate analysis, knowledge of the RSV vaccine was the only factor independently associated with vaccination coverage (adjusted OR: 3.4; 95% CI: 1.9-6.2; p <0.001). RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women was lower than that for other vaccines recommended during pregnancy. We identified limited vaccine availability and limited knowledge about the vaccine as factors associated with non-vaccination. Strengthening information and recommendations during prenatal care could help improve vaccination coverage. This study provides a validated tool for assessing barriers to vaccination among pregnant women.
abstract_zh: 阿根廷于 2024 年引入针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的孕产妇 疫苗接种,以预防婴儿严重呼吸道感染。为了确保令人满意的 疫苗接种 率,识别其实施的障碍非常重要。确定孕妇中 RSV 疫苗接种 的障碍。我们估计了 RSV 疫苗接种 覆盖范围以及覆盖范围和障碍之间的潜在关联。人口和方法。这是一项基于对有资格接受 RSV 疫苗 的母亲的调查的横断面研究。我们开发并验证了一种工具来识别结构、信息、情感和社交障碍。我们使用逻辑回归进行单变量和多变量分析。我们调查了 216 名母亲。RSV 疫苗 覆盖率为 43.7%。在单变量分析中,少于 5 次产前检查和未收到明确信息与较低的 疫苗接种 率相关。在多变量分析中,RSV 疫苗 的知识是与 ZX​​QTERMKQXZ 覆盖率独立相关的唯一因素(调整后 OR:3.4;95% CI:1.9-6.2;p <0.001)。孕妇中 RSV 疫苗接种 的覆盖率低于怀孕期间推荐的其他 疫苗 的覆盖率。我们将有限的 疫苗 可用性和有限的 疫苗 知识确定为与非 疫苗 相关的因素。加强产前护理期间的信息和建议有助于提高 疫苗接种 的覆盖率。这项研究提供了一个经过验证的工具,用于评估孕妇 疫苗接种 的障碍。

title: Rise of Lower Respiratory Tract Infections Other than Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Emergency Room: Results from the Season (2024/25) of the RISE Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) are a major cause of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations. Although respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and rhinovirus (RV) are common etiological agents, pathogen-specific data from pediatric emergency settings remain limited. METHODS: This prospective surveillance study quantified ARI-related ED visits, described pathogen-specific epidemiology, and assessed attendance and hospitalization rates as well as the distribution of lower versus upper respiratory tract infections (LRTI/URTI) in children younger than 60 months in two pediatric EDs in Berlin between November 1, 2024 and May 31, 2025. Respiratory pathogens were identified using nasopharyngeal swab samples tested by multiplex real-time RT-PCR (QIAstat-Dx® Respiratory Panel Plus). RESULTS: Within the study period 4042 ARI-related ED visits occurred. A total of 310 children were enrolled in our study (median age 18 months); 115 (37.1%) had LRTI and 195 (62.9%) URTI. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 271 children (87.4%). The attendance rate for RSV was 24.4% (66 cases), for FLU 25.8% (70 cases), and for RV 29.5% (80 cases). Overall, 93 children (30.0%) were hospitalized, including 65 with LRTI and 28 with URTI. Hospitalization rates were highest for RSV infections (26/65, 40.0%) and RV infections (28/65, 43.1%), and lower for FLU infections (13/69, 18.8%). Hospitalization due to LRTI predominated among children with RSV (24/26, 92.3%) and RV infections (20/28, 71.4%), whereas FLU infections were less frequently observed (7/13, 53.9%). Furthermore, younger age, a history of pneumonia, a history of bronchiolitis, and the absence of breastfeeding were associated with hospitalization. CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to the previous season, in which RSV was associated with the highest attendance and hospitalization rate, we observed a high burden of RV infections in the 2024/2025 season. These findings may impact surveillance strategies, clinical management, and future public health strategies.

title: Respiratory syncytial virus in adults aged ≥ 50 years in the Netherlands: a database and time-series modelling analysis (2013-2020).
abstract: Abstract Purpose Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant yet historically understudied contributor to acute respiratory infection (ARI) in older adults. This study aimed to quantify ARI-associated hospital admissions and estimate RSV-related burden of disease in secondary care in the Netherlands using time-series modelling. Methods This retrospective cohort study (1 July 2013 to 29 February 2020) utilised routinely collected primary and secondary care data from the PHARMO Data Network. ARI-associated hospital admissions in patients aged ≥ 50 years, identified via International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes, were described in terms of patient and clinical characteristics and healthcare resource utilisation. The number and annual rate of RSV- and influenza-associated ARI and lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) hospital admissions by age and risk group were estimated using a Quasi-Poisson regression model. Results There were 97,279 ARI admissions in 63,420 patients. Estimated RSV-associated ARI hospital admission rates ranged from 0.70/1,000 person-years (PY) to 1.92/1,000 PY in adults aged ≥ 50 and ≥ 75, respectively. RSV-associated LRTD admissions varied from 0.63/1,000 PY to 1.73/1,000 PY in these groups. Hospitalisation rates were higher in high-risk individuals. Estimated RSV admissions were up to six times higher than observed. During peak months, up to 30% of ARI (20% of LRTD) admissions were attributable to RSV. RSV-coded admissions had an average length of stay of 7–8 days, and 30% of patients experienced all-cause readmission within 90 days. Conclusion The substantial hospitalisation burden of RSV calls for prioritisation of RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination, alongside influenza and other causes of ARI and LRTD.

analysis_zh.methods: 使用准泊松回归模型估算了按年龄和风险组划分的 RSV 和流感相关 ARI 和下呼吸道疾病 (LRTD) 住院人数和年发生率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 63,420 名患者中有 97,279 名 ARI 入院。年龄≥ 50 岁和≥ 75 岁的成年人中,RSV 相关 ARI 入院率估计范围分别为 0.70/1,000 人年 (PY) 至 1.92/1,000 PY。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究对 50 岁以上成年人与 RSV 相关的入院情况进行了新的估计,强调了该人群中 RSV 造成的巨大负担。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要采取有针对性的 RSV 预防策略,特别是对于高危人群,以减少与 RSV 相关的住院负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于常规收集的数据,并未考虑潜在的漏报情况,这可能会影响估计 RSV 入院人数的准确性。

title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to share lessons from the rapid implementation of RSV prevention products and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. The research was needed to address the challenge of integrating new RSV prevention strategies into routine clinical practice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable monoclonal antibody nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals within the Sydney Local Health District. The study period spanned from February to September 2025, focusing on immunisation uptake among mothers and eligible newborns.
analysis.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to evaluate the rollout process and identify factors influencing immunisation uptake.
analysis.main_results: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in the two hospitals increased from 4% in the first month of rollout to 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reasons for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that coordinated engagement with multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for successful program rollout. The study highlights the importance of clear messaging and systemic safeguards in implementing multiple immunisation products for distinct groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of future RSV prevention programs by demonstrating the effectiveness of strategies such as clinician education and integration of immunisation into medical record workflows. They also provide insights into improving uptake and reducing refusal rates for RSV vaccines and monoclonal antibodies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on deidentified summary data and the absence of recorded reasons for refusal. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the descriptive nature of the analysis and the lack of detailed statistical or causal interpretations.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, including the maternal vaccine and the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab, in two maternity hospitals in Sydney, Australia. It reports that RSV vaccination coverage among mothers improved significantly from 4% in February 2025 to 70-74% by September 2025. As coverage increased, fewer newborns required nirsevimab. However, 36% of eligible families declined the antibody, with no recorded reasons. The study highlights the importance of multidisciplinary engagement and clear messaging in program implementation. It also notes that integrating immunisation into medical record workflows can support program adoption. The findings suggest that while the rollout was successful, the lack of detailed refusal data and the descriptive nature of the analysis limit the strength of the evidence. These insights can inform future RSV prevention strategies and improve immunisation uptake.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。这项研究需要解决将新的 RSV 预防策略纳入常规临床实践的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在悉尼地方卫生区的两家妇产医院推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗。该研究时间跨度为 2025 年 2 月至 9 月,重点关注母亲和符合条件的新生儿的免疫接种情况。
elements_zh.methods: 来自电子病历的去识别化摘要数据被描述性地分析为计数和比例。实施研究综合框架用于评估推广过程并确定影响免疫接种的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV 疫苗接种 在两家医院分娩的妇女的覆盖率从推出第一个月的 4% 增加到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,拒绝的原因没有记录。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明多学科领导者和临床医生的协调参与对于项目的成功推出至关重要。该研究强调了在针对不同群体实施多种免疫产品时,明确的信息传递和系统保障措施的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过证明临床医生教育和将免疫接种纳入医疗记录工作流程等策略的有效性,为未来 RSV 预防计划的发展提供信息。他们还提供了有关提高 RSV 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的吸收率和降低拒绝率的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于未识别身份的汇总数据,并且没有记录拒绝的原因。由于分析的描述性以及缺乏详细的统计或因果解释,证据的强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。这项研究需要解决将新的 RSV 预防策略纳入常规临床实践的挑战。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在悉尼地方卫生区的两家妇产医院推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗。该研究时间跨度为 2025 年 2 月至 9 月,重点关注母亲和符合条件的新生儿的免疫接种情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 来自电子病历的去识别化摘要数据被描述性地分析为计数和比例。实施研究综合框架用于评估推广过程并确定影响免疫接种的因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: RSV 疫苗接种 在两家医院分娩的妇女的覆盖率从推出第一个月的 4% 增加到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,拒绝的原因没有记录。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明多学科领导者和临床医生的协调参与对于项目的成功推出至关重要。该研究强调了在针对不同群体实施多种免疫产品时,明确的信息传递和系统保障措施的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过证明临床医生教育和将免疫接种纳入医疗记录工作流程等策略的有效性,为未来 RSV 预防计划的发展提供信息。他们还提供了有关提高 RSV 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的吸收率和降低拒绝率的见解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于未识别身份的汇总数据,并且没有记录拒绝的原因。由于分析的描述性以及缺乏详细的统计或因果解释,证据的强度中等。

title: Fulminant necrotizing enterocolitis associated with severe RSV infection in a preterm infant following Nirsevimab prophylaxis: a case report.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis with the monoclonal antibody Nirsevimab has shown high efficacy in preventing severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants. However, the sequences of immunopathological phenomena leading to breakthrough infections and the role of RSV in causing extrapulmonary disease remain poorly understood. We report on a former preterm infant who developed an unusually severe form of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) requiring multiple emergency laparotomies and prolonged intensive care treatment in the context of severe RSV-bronchiolitis 22 days after passive immunization with Nirsevimab. RSV RNA was retrospectively detected using a validated RSV PCR assay in resected intestinal tissue obtained during the acute disease phase but was not detected in tissue collected during later surgical reconstruction. Our case highlights the need for clinicians to maintain a high index of suspicion for intestinal complications in infants with severe RSV infection. Although these findings raise the possibility of intestinal RSV involvement, a causal relationship between Nirsevimab prophylaxis, antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and NEC cannot be established from this single case. Confirmation in additional clinical and translational studies is required. Further clinical and translational studies are required to clarify the potential role of RSV in intestinal disease and the mechanisms underlying severe breakthrough infections.

title_zh: 病例报告 预防后早产儿发生与严重 RSV 感染相关的暴发性坏死性小肠结肠炎:病例报告。
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis with the monoclonal antibody Nirsevimab has shown high efficacy in preventing severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants. However, the sequences of immunopathological phenomena leading to breakthrough infections and the role of RSV in causing extrapulmonary disease remain poorly understood. We report on a former preterm infant who developed an unusually severe form of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) requiring multiple emergency laparotomies and prolonged intensive care treatment in the context of severe RSV-bronchiolitis 22 days after passive immunization with Nirsevimab. RSV RNA was retrospectively detected using a validated RSV PCR assay in resected intestinal tissue obtained during the acute disease phase but was not detected in tissue collected during later surgical reconstruction. Our case highlights the need for clinicians to maintain a high index of suspicion for intestinal complications in infants with severe RSV infection. Although these findings raise the possibility of intestinal RSV involvement, a causal relationship between Nirsevimab prophylaxis, antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and NEC cannot be established from this single case. Confirmation in additional clinical and translational studies is required. Further clinical and translational studies are required to clarify the potential role of RSV in intestinal disease and the mechanisms underlying severe breakthrough infections.
abstract_zh: 使用单克隆抗体 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预防在预防婴儿严重下呼吸道感染方面显示出高效。然而,导致突破性感染的免疫病理学现象的序列以及 RSV 在引起肺外疾病中的作用仍然知之甚少。我们报告了一名早产儿,在使用 尼塞韦单抗 被动免疫 22 天后,在严重 RSV-毛细支气管炎 的情况下,出现了异常严重的坏死性小肠结肠炎 (NEC),需要多次紧急剖腹手术和长期重症监护 治疗。使用经过验证的 RSV PCR 检测在急性疾病期获得的切除肠道组织中回顾性检测到 RSV RNA,但在随后的手术重建期间收集的组织中未检测到 RSV RNA。我们的病例强调临床医生需要对严重 RSV 感染婴儿的肠道并发症保持高度怀疑。尽管这些发现提出了肠道 RSV 受累的可能性,但从这一单一病例中无法确定 尼塞韦单抗 预防、抗体依赖性增强 (ADE) 和 NEC 之间的因果关系。需要更多临床和转化研究的证实。需要进一步的临床和转化研究来阐明 RSV 在肠道疾病中的潜在作用以及严重突破性感染的机制。

title: Secondary Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis after Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in the Setting of an Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection: A Case Report.
abstract: Secondary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (SPAP) is rare and often results in poor outcomes; therefore, it is crucial to diagnose and treat it appropriately. A 23-year-old man who received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) 18 months before presentation was diagnosed with SPAP after allo-HSCT in the setting of an RSV infection. The patient's respiratory symptoms improved after treatment for RSV infection, and SPAP gradually improved during the follow-up period. This case suggests that SPAP should be considered in post-HSCT patients with persistent respiratory symptoms or radiological abnormalities in the setting of an RSV infection.

title: Validation of Small-Molecule Entry Inhibitors Targeting the Respiratory Syncytial Virus.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe respiratory infections worldwide, particularly in infants, young children, and elderly individuals. Despite the availability of preventive options such as vaccines and monoclonal antibodies, effective antiviral therapies for acute infections remain limited. Therefore, we investigated small-molecule entry inhibitors identified in a high-throughput campaing and evaluated the most promising candidates in detail by performing resynthesis and determining their antiviral activity. Unfortunately, analytical investigations by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) revealed discrepancies between the screening samples and the resynthesized compounds for two compound classes, highlighting the complexity of hit validation and the potential influence of impurities. By publishing these results, we aim not only to underscore the importance of rigorous analytical and biological validation in screening campaigns but also to support the development of improved strategies for identifying reliable RSV inhibitors. We also believe it is important to publish false-positive hits to avoid time efforts on projects that assume such compounds as genuine hits.

title: Maternal Vaccination vs Nirsevimab Use and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection Among Full-Term Infants
abstract: Importance: Since 2023, infants can be protected from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) through a vaccine (RSVpreF) for pregnant persons or a monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) for infants. Objective: To assess the relative product effectiveness (rPE) of maternal RSVpreF vs infant nirsevimab against RSV infection and hospitalization among infants born in the 2023 to 2025 RSV seasons. Design, Setting, and Participants: This retrospective cohort study included full-term infants born at Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC), an integrated health care system with approximately 40 000 births each year, from December 3, 2023, to March 30, 2024, or September 29, 2024, to March 15, 2025. Infants protected by RSVpreF were matched to infants protected with nirsevimab with optimal full matching (up to 1:5), adjusting for birth week, sex, and maternal factors. Each group was also compared with infants with no protection, matching unprotected infants to both RSVpreF and nirsevimab infants (up to 1:10). Exposures: Maternal RSVpreF at 32 to 36 weeks' gestation or infant nirsevimab through age 7 days. Main Outcomes and Measures: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed RSV and RSV hospitalization (PCR-confirmed RSV 10 days before to 7 days after hospitalization) in infants aged 8 to 180 days or through RSV season end (April 30 in both seasons). rPE was estimated from age 8 to 180 days using restricted mean time lost. Results: Of 15 124 matched infants (7729 [51.1%] male) in the primary analysis, 146 (0.97%) had RSV infection (106 of 11 293 [0.94%] in RSVpreF group and 40 of 3831 [1.04%] in nirsevimab group) and 12 (0.08%) were hospitalized (7 [0.06%] in RSVpreF group and 5 [0.13%] in nirsevimab group). The rPE of RSVpreF vs nirsevimab was -5.3% (95% CI, -44.8% to 23.4%) against infection and 61.5% (95% CI, -10.8% to 86.7%) against hospitalization. Compared with no protection, RSVpreF rPE was 69.3% (95% CI, 59.9% to 76.6%) against infection and 86.4% (95% CI, 66.4% to 94.5%) against hospitalization; nirsevimab rPE was 65.2% (95% CI, 51.0%-75.4%) and 73.8% (95% CI, 33.4%-89.7%), respectively. Conclusion: In this cohort study of infants born in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons, no statistically significant difference between maternal RSVpreF and infant nirsevimab in RSV infection or hospitalization was detected. Compared with no protection, both products were associated with fewer infections and hospitalizations. This study supports current US guidelines for either maternal RSVpreF or infant nirsevimab to protect all infants from RSV.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估使用 RSVpreF 的母亲 疫苗接种 与婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 在预防 2023 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节出生的足月婴儿 RSV 感染和住院方面的相对有效性。自2023年起,婴儿可以通过母体疫苗接种或婴儿单克隆抗体治疗来保护婴儿免受RSV感染。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性 队列研究 研究纳入了 2023 年 12 月 3 日至 2024 年 3 月 30 日或 2024 年 9 月 29 日至 2025 年 3 月 15 日在北加州 Kaiser Permanente 出生的足月婴儿。婴儿根据出生周、性别和母亲因素进行匹配,RSVpreF 与 尼塞韦单抗 的最佳完全匹配(高达 1:5)对于未受保护的婴儿,最多为 1:10。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 PCR 确认的 RSV 感染和住院作为主要结局。暴露是妊娠 32 至 36 周时的母亲 RSVpreF 或婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 至 7 天的暴露。主要结果指标是限制 8 至 180 天婴儿或 RSV 季节结束(两个季节均为 4 月 30 日)期间因感染和住院而损失的平均时间。
elements_zh.main_results: 在15,124例匹配的婴儿中,有146例(0.97%)出现呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染(其中RSVpreF组106例,尼塞韦单抗组40例),有12例(0.08%)住院治疗(其中RSVpreF组7例,尼塞韦单抗组5例)。RSVpreF与尼塞韦单抗相比,对感染的相对预防效果(rPE)为-5.3%(95%置信区间:-44.8%至23.4%),对住院的相对预防效果为61.5%(95%置信区间:-10.8%至86.7%)。与无保护相比,RSVpreF将感染率降低了69.3%(95%置信区间:59.9%至76.6%),将住院率降低了86.4%(95%置信区间:66.4%至94.5%);尼塞韦单抗分别将感染率降低了65.2%(95%置信区间:51.0%至75.4%)和住院率降低了73.8%(95%置信区间:33.4%至89.7%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,母亲RSVpreF和婴儿尼塞韦单抗在RSV感染或住院方面没有统计学上的显着差异。与没有保护的情况相比,这两种产品都可以减少感染和住院治疗。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究支持美国现行的母亲 RSVpreF 或婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 指南,以保护所有婴儿免受 RSV 感染,表明这两种方法都能有效降低 RSV 感染率和住院率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的未测量混杂因素而受到限制。样本量足以进行初步分析,但 rPE 估计值的置信区间很宽,表明结果存在一定的不确定性。

Objective: To assess the relative product effectiveness (rPE) of maternal RSVpreF vs infant nirsevimab against RSV infection and hospitalization among infants born in the 2023 to 2025 RSV seasons. Design, Setting, and Participants: This retrospective cohort study included full-term infants born at Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC), an integrated health care system with approximately 40 000 births each year, from December 3, 2023, to March 30, 2024, or September 29, 2024, to March 15, 2025. Infants protected by RSVpreF were matched to infants protected with nirsevimab with optimal full matching (up to 1:5), adjusting for birth week, sex, and maternal factors. Each group was also compared with infants with no protection, matching unprotected infants to both RSVpreF and nirsevimab infants (up to 1:10). Exposures: Maternal RSVpreF at 32 to 36 weeks' gestation or infant nirsevimab through age 7 days. Main Outcomes and Measures: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed RSV and RSV hospitalization (PCR-confirmed RSV 10 days before to 7 days after hospitalization) in infants aged 8 to 180 days or through RSV season end (April 30 in both seasons). rPE was estimated from age 8 to 180 days using restricted mean time lost. Results: Of 15 124 matched infants (7729 [51.1%] male) in the primary analysis, 146 (0.97%) had RSV infection (106 of 11 293 [0.94%] in RSVpreF group and 40 of 3831 [1.04%] in nirsevimab group) and 12 (0.08%) were hospitalized (7 [0.06%] in RSVpreF group and 5 [0.13%] in nirsevimab group). The rPE of RSVpreF vs nirsevimab was -5.3% (95% CI, -44.8% to 23.4%) against infection and 61.5% (95% CI, -10.8% to 86.7%) against hospitalization. Compared with no protection, RSVpreF rPE was 69.3% (95% CI, 59.9% to 76.6%) against infection and 86.4% (95% CI, 66.4% to 94.5%) against hospitalization; nirsevimab rPE was 65.2% (95% CI, 51.0%-75.4%) and 73.8% (95% CI, 33.4%-89.7%), respectively. Conclusion: In this cohort study of infants born in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons, no statistically significant difference between maternal RSVpreF and infant nirsevimab in RSV infection or hospitalization was detected. Compared with no protection, both products were associated with fewer infections and hospitalizations. This study supports current US guidelines for either maternal RSVpreF or infant nirsevimab to protect all infants from RSV.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估使用 RSVpreF 的母亲 疫苗接种 与婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 在预防 2023 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节出生的足月婴儿 RSV 感染和住院方面的相对有效性。自2023年起,婴儿可以通过母体疫苗接种或婴儿单克隆抗体治疗来保护婴儿免受RSV感染。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性 队列研究 研究纳入了 2023 年 12 月 3 日至 2024 年 3 月 30 日或 2024 年 9 月 29 日至 2025 年 3 月 15 日在北加州 Kaiser Permanente 出生的足月婴儿。婴儿根据出生周、性别和母亲因素进行匹配,RSVpreF 与 尼塞韦单抗 的最佳完全匹配(高达 1:5)对于未受保护的婴儿,最多为 1:10。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用 PCR 确认的 RSV 感染和住院作为主要结局。暴露是妊娠 32 至 36 周时的母亲 RSVpreF 或婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 至 7 天的暴露。主要结果指标是限制 8 至 180 天婴儿或 RSV 季节结束(两个季节均为 4 月 30 日)期间因感染和住院而损失的平均时间。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在15,124例匹配的婴儿中,有146例(0.97%)出现呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染(其中RSVpreF组106例,尼塞韦单抗组40例),有12例(0.08%)住院治疗(其中RSVpreF组7例,尼塞韦单抗组5例)。RSVpreF与尼塞韦单抗相比,对感染的相对预防效果(rPE)为-5.3%(95%置信区间:-44.8%至23.4%),对住院的相对预防效果为61.5%(95%置信区间:-10.8%至86.7%)。与无保护相比,RSVpreF将感染率降低了69.3%(95%置信区间:59.9%至76.6%),将住院率降低了86.4%(95%置信区间:66.4%至94.5%);尼塞韦单抗分别将感染率降低了65.2%(95%置信区间:51.0%至75.4%)和住院率降低了73.8%(95%置信区间:33.4%至89.7%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,母亲RSVpreF和婴儿尼塞韦单抗在RSV感染或住院方面没有统计学上的显着差异。与没有保护的情况相比,这两种产品都可以减少感染和住院治疗。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究支持美国现行的母亲 RSVpreF 或婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 指南,以保护所有婴儿免受 RSV 感染,表明这两种方法都能有效降低 RSV 感染率和住院率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的未测量混杂因素而受到限制。样本量足以进行初步分析,但 rPE 估计值的置信区间很宽,表明结果存在一定的不确定性。

title: Epidemiology and seasonality of respiratory syncytial virus among hospitalized pediatric patients with lower respiratory tract infections in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia (2017–2024)
abstract: Background Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant public health concern globally, with distinct seasonal patterns in temperate regions, while tropical settings experience RSV year-round with seasonal fluctuations. This study investigated seasonality and exogenous factors influencing RSV cases among hospitalized children under 12 years in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. Methods Weekly laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases among hospitalized pediatric patients presenting with acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) across 417 continuous WHO epidemiological weeks (EpiWeek 1, 2017 to EpiWeek 52, 2024) were analyzed using decomposition and autocorrelation functions. Relationships between RSV and co-circulating viruses, meteorological variables, and holidays were assessed via cross-correlation and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (ARIMAX) modeling. Results A total of 6,545 (14.29%) samples were RSV-positive from a total of 45,817 tested. Historical peaks (July–September) were disrupted during 2020–2023 but re-established in 2024. The ARIMAX (2,0,4) (1,0,0) 52 model revealed that RSV dynamics were driven primarily by internal autoregressive patterns rather than meteorological factors. Major public holidays exhibited a significant dual effect, with an immediate decrease in reported cases ( p = 0.012) followed by a significant surge ( p = 0.014). Influenza activity was a significant predictor with a one-week lag ( p = 0.012). Conclusion The pandemic temporarily shifted RSV seasonality, which has since normalized. The associations with holiday periods and influenza activity suggests that behavioral factors and viral interference may influence RSV circulation. These findings emphasize the need for dynamic surveillance to optimize the timing of future RSV immunizations in Malaysia.

title_zh: 马来西亚森美兰州住院下呼吸道感染儿科患者的 流行病学 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 的季节性(2017-2024 年)
source_body_en: Background Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant public health concern globally, with distinct seasonal patterns in temperate regions, while tropical settings experience RSV year-round with seasonal fluctuations. This study investigated seasonality and exogenous factors influencing RSV cases among hospitalized children under 12 years in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. Methods Weekly laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases among hospitalized pediatric patients presenting with acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) across 417 continuous WHO epidemiological weeks (EpiWeek 1, 2017 to EpiWeek 52, 2024) were analyzed using decomposition and autocorrelation functions. Relationships between RSV and co-circulating viruses, meteorological variables, and holidays were assessed via cross-correlation and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (ARIMAX) modeling. Results A total of 6,545 (14.29%) samples were RSV-positive from a total of 45,817 tested. Historical peaks (July–September) were disrupted during 2020–2023 but re-established in 2024. The ARIMAX (2,0,4) (1,0,0) 52 model revealed that RSV dynamics were driven primarily by internal autoregressive patterns rather than meteorological factors. Major public holidays exhibited a significant dual effect, with an immediate decrease in reported cases ( p = 0.012) followed by a significant surge ( p = 0.014). Influenza activity was a significant predictor with a one-week lag ( p = 0.012). Conclusion The pandemic temporarily shifted RSV seasonality, which has since normalized. The associations with holiday periods and influenza activity suggests that behavioral factors and viral interference may influence RSV circulation. These findings emphasize the need for dynamic surveillance to optimize the timing of future RSV immunizations in Malaysia.
abstract_zh: 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然是全球重大的公共卫生问题,温带地区具有明显的季节性模式,而热带地区全年都会经历 RSV 并伴有季节性波动。本研究调查了影响马来西亚森美兰州 12 岁以下住院儿童 RSV 病例的季节性和外源性因素。方法 使用分解和自相关函数对 417 个连续 WHO 流行病学周(2017 年第 1 周到 2024 年第 52 周)住院儿科患者中出现急性下呼吸道感染 (LRTI) 的每周实验室确诊的 RSV 阳性病例进行分析。通过互相关和外生变量自回归综合移动平均 (ARIMAX) 模型评估 RSV 与共循环病毒、气象变量和假期之间的关系。结果 在总共 45,817 份检测中,共有 6,545 份 (14.29%) 样本呈 RSV 阳性。历史峰值(7 月至 9 月)在 2020 年至 2023 年期间被破坏,但在 2024 年重新建立。ARIMAX (2,0,4) (1,0,0) 52 模型显示,RSV 动态主要由内部自回归模式驱动,而不是气象因素。主要公众假期表现出显着的双重效应,报告病例数立即下降 (p = 0.012),随后显着激增 (p = 0.014)。流感活动是一个滞后一周的重要预测因素 (p = 0.012)。结论 大流行暂时改变了 RSV 的季节性,此后已恢复正常。与假期和流感活动的关联表明,行为因素和病毒干扰可能会影响 RSV 循环。这些发现强调需要动态 监测 来优化马来西亚未来 RSV 免疫接种的时间。

title: Age-Related Differences in the Clinical Presentation of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Hospitalized Children: A Three-Year Retrospective Study
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of hospitalization in infants and young children, with the highest risk of severe disease occurring during early infancy. Age may influence not only disease severity but also the clinical phenotype of RSV infection. This study aimed to evaluate age-related differences in clinical presentation and respiratory severity among children hospitalized with RSV infection. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including 241 children aged 0–24 months hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations were compared across four age groups (0–3, 4–6, 7–12, and 13–24 months). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between exact age in months and individual clinical manifestations, adjusting for sex, prematurity, documented viral co-infection and feeding type. The Holm procedure was applied to account for multiple comparisons in the exact-age analyses. Supplemental oxygen requirement was evaluated as a marker of respiratory severity. Results: Fever increased significantly with age, from 48.8% among children aged 0–3 months to 81.7% among those aged 13–24 months (p < 0.001). In adjusted analyses, each additional month of age was associated with higher odds of fever (aOR 1.090, 95% CI 1.045–1.137; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and lower odds of thoracoabdominal asynchrony (aOR 0.951, 95% CI 0.917–0.986; Holm-adjusted p = 0.044). Associations with tachypnea/polypnea and intercostal/subcostal retractions did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Supplemental oxygen was required in 29.0% of patients. Infants aged 0–3 months required oxygen more frequently than older children (46.5% vs. 25.3%) and had significantly higher adjusted odds of oxygen requirement (aOR 2.54, 95% CI 1.26–5.0; p = 0.009). Conclusions: The clinical phenotype and respiratory severity of RSV infection may vary s with age during the first two years of life. Younger infants exhibit more prominent signs of respiratory distress despite a lower frequency of fever, and infants aged 0–3 months have a particularly high likelihood of requiring supplemental oxygen. These findings highlight the importance of age-specific clinical assessment and reinforce the vulnerability of infants during the earliest months of life.

title: A Review of Changing Patterns of Pediatric Respiratory Infections in the Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Era: A Global and Indian Perspective
abstract: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of illness in children, and their epidemiology has changed noticeably during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Non-pharmaceutical interventions, including masking, school closure, distancing, improved hand hygiene, and reduced travel, were associated with a fall in several common respiratory viruses, particularly influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), while rhinovirus/enterovirus continued to circulate in many settings. After restrictions were relaxed, many countries reported delayed or out-of-season activity of RSV, influenza, human metapneumovirus, and other respiratory pathogens. Multiplex molecular platforms such as the BioFire Respiratory Panel have helped document these shifts by enabling rapid, simultaneous detection of multiple viral and bacterial agents. This narrative review summarizes pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic respiratory pathogen patterns with emphasis on pediatric infections, global observations, and Indian data. It also discusses the role of immunity gaps, disrupted routine immunization, altered healthcare-seeking behavior, co-detection, and regional variation in India. Strengthening respiratory virus surveillance, improving access to multiplex diagnostics in sentinel centers, restoring routine immunization, and integrating influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 prevention strategies into pediatric public health planning are essential in the post-COVID period.

title: MUC5B Expression Is Associated with Reduced Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection and Pulmonary Inflammation
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract disease, particularly in infants and older adults. During RSV infection, excessive secretion and accumulation of gel-forming mucins can obstruct the small airways and contribute to pulmonary pathology. However, airway mucins also form a first-line barrier that traps inhaled pathogens and limits their access to the airway epithelium. Whether MUC5B, a major secreted mucin in the lower respiratory tract, influences RSV infection and associated pulmonary responses remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of MUC5B during RSV infection using human A549 epithelial cells stably overexpressing MUC5B and female Muc5b-deficient mice. MUC5B overexpression significantly reduced intracellular RSV RNA levels following infection with the A2, Long, and B1 strains. In vivo, Muc5b−/− mice exhibited substantially higher pulmonary RSV RNA burdens at 5 days post-infection, whereas no significant genotype-dependent differences were detected in the nasal turbinates. Muc5b deficiency was also associated with more severe respiratory tract pathology and a higher proportion of pulmonary neutrophils after RSV infection. Eosinophil proportions increased after infection in both wild-type and Muc5b−/− mice, whereas the proportions of alveolar macrophages decreased and those of interstitial macrophages increased in both genotypes. Collectively, these findings suggest that, despite the established contribution of excessive mucus accumulation to airway obstruction, MUC5B also has a protective role during RSV infection. MUC5B may enhance pulmonary resistance to RSV by contributing to airway barrier function, reducing pulmonary viral burden, limiting tissue injury, and attenuating neutrophilic inflammation. These findings identify MUC5B as an important component of mucosal antiviral defense and broaden our understanding of how airway mucins influence susceptibility to RSV infection.

source_records.title: MUC5B Expression Is Associated with Reduced Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection and Pulmonary Inflammation
source_records.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract disease, particularly in infants and older adults. During RSV infection, excessive secretion and accumulation of gel-forming mucins can obstruct the small airways and contribute to pulmonary pathology. However, airway mucins also form a first-line barrier that traps inhaled pathogens and limits their access to the airway epithelium. Whether MUC5B, a major secreted mucin in the lower respiratory tract, influences RSV infection and associated pulmonary responses remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of MUC5B during RSV infection using human A549 epithelial cells stably overexpressing MUC5B and female Muc5b-deficient mice. MUC5B overexpression significantly reduced intracellular RSV RNA levels following infection with the A2, Long, and B1 strains. In vivo, Muc5b−/− mice exhibited substantially higher pulmonary RSV RNA burdens at 5 days post-infection, whereas no significant genotype-dependent differences were detected in the nasal turbinates. Eosinophil proportions increased after infection in both wild-type and Muc5b−/− mice, whereas the proportions of alveolar macrophages decreased and those of interstitial macrophages increased in both genotypes. MUC5B may enhance pulmonary resistance to RSV by contributing to airway barrier function, reducing pulmonary viral burden, limiting tissue injury, and attenuating neutrophilic inflammation. These findings identify MUC5B as an important component of mucosal antiviral defense and broaden our understanding of how airway mucins influence susceptibility to RSV infection.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是严重下呼吸道疾病的主要原因,特别是在婴儿和老年人中。RSV 感染期间,凝胶形成粘蛋白的过度分泌和积聚会阻塞小气道并导致肺部病变。然而,气道粘蛋白也形成一线屏障,捕获吸入的病原体并限制其进入气道上皮。MUC5B(下呼吸道的一种主要分泌粘蛋白)是否影响 RSV 感染和相关的肺部反应仍知之甚少。在这里,我们使用稳定过表达 MUC5B 的人 A549 上皮细胞和雌性 Muc5b 缺陷小鼠研究了 MUC5B 在 RSV 感染过程中的作用。A2、Long 和 B1 毒株感染后,MUC5B 过表达显着降低了细胞内 RSV RNA 水平。在体内,Muc5b−/− 小鼠在感染后 5 天表现出明显更高的肺部 RSV RNA 负荷,而在鼻甲中没有检测到显着的基因型依赖性差异。Muc5b 缺乏还与 RSV 感染后更严重的呼吸道病理和更高比例的肺部中性粒细胞有关。野生型和 Muc5b−/− 小鼠感染后嗜酸性粒细胞比例均增加,而两种基因型的肺泡巨噬细胞比例均减少,间质巨噬细胞比例均增加。总的来说,这些发现表明,尽管粘液过多积聚已确定会导致气道阻塞,但 MUC5B 在 RSV 感染期间也具有保护作用。MUC5B 可能通过促进气道屏障功能、减少肺部病毒负荷、限制组织损伤和减轻中性粒细胞炎症来增强肺部对 RSV 的抵抗力。这些发现将 MUC5B 确定为粘膜 抗病毒药物 防御的重要组成部分,并拓宽了我们对气道粘蛋白如何影响 RSV 感染易感性的理解。

title: The molecular epidemiology of human respiratory syncytial virus in a tertiary paediatric hospital between 2020 and 2024
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory illness in young children, contributing significantly to morbidity and mortality and placing a substantial burden on resource-limited healthcare systems. Molecular epidemiological data from sub-Saharan Africa remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the genetic diversity and evolution of RSV in a paediatric population in Cape Town, South Africa, from September 2020 to June 2024. Methods: Respiratory syncytial virus-positive respiratory samples with a cycle threshold (Ct)
journal: Journal of the Colleges of Medicine of South Africa

title: Temporal changes in pediatric respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus positivity across COVID-19-related periods: A six-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective: To describe temporal changes in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and adenovirus positivity among children tested across three COVID-19-related periods.Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 8,253 children aged 0–18 years who underwent concurrent RSV and adenovirus antigen testing for suspected acute respiratory infection from January 2018 through June 2023. Periods were defined as pre-pandemic (January 2018–February 2020), restrictive pandemic (March 2020–May 2021), and post-restriction (June 2021–June 2023). Positivity proportions were compared by period. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated from period-specific counts using the pre-pandemic period as reference.Results: RSV was detected in 266 children (3.2%) and adenovirus in 612 (7.4%). RSV positivity was 1.5% (55/3,785) pre-pandemic, 1.2% (13/1,055) during restrictions, and 5.8% (198/3,413) post-restriction. Relative to the pre-pandemic period, the odds of RSV positivity did not differ during restrictions (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.46–1.55) but were higher post-restriction (OR 4.18, 95% CI 3.09–5.65). Adenovirus positivity was 8.8%, 10.2%, and 5.0%, respectively; corresponding ORs were 1.18 (95% CI 0.94–1.48) and 0.54 (95% CI 0.45–0.66).Conclusion: Among clinically selected children who were tested, RSV and adenovirus positivity followed different temporal patterns. These unadjusted associations should not be interpreted as causal effects of specific public-health measures because seasonality, testing practices, and healthcare-seeking behavior may have differed across periods.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate how the positivity rates of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and adenovirus changed over time among children during three distinct periods related to the COVID-19 pandemic, addressing the need to understand the impact of public health measures on these viral infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted across three periods: pre-pandemic (January 2018–February 2020), restrictive pandemic (March 2020–May 2021), and post-restriction (June 2021–June 2023). It included 8,253 children aged 0–18 years who underwent concurrent RSV and adenovirus antigen testing for suspected acute respiratory infection.
analysis.methods: Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated from period-specific counts using the pre-pandemic period as reference. Positivity proportions were compared by period, with the pre-pandemic period serving as the baseline for analysis.
analysis.main_results: RSV was detected in 266 children (3.2%) and adenovirus in 612 (7.4%). RSV positivity was 1.5% (55/3,785) pre-pandemic, 1.2% (13/1,055) during restrictions, and 5.8% (198/3,413) post-restriction. Adenovirus positivity was 8.8%, 10.2%, and 5.0%, respectively, with corresponding ORs of 1.18 (95% CI 0.94–1.48) and 0.54 (95% CI 0.45–0.66) relative to the pre-pandemic period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RSV and adenovirus positivity followed different temporal patterns, with RSV positivity increasing significantly post-restriction compared to the pre-pandemic period, while adenovirus positivity showed a decrease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that changes in public health measures and healthcare-seeking behavior may have influenced RSV positivity rates, which could inform future surveillance and intervention strategies for pediatric respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on unadjusted odds ratios and potential confounding factors such as seasonality and testing practices. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single-center retrospective analysis without controlling for these variables.

analysis.summary_en: This six-year retrospective cohort study examined temporal changes in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and adenovirus positivity among children during three distinct periods related to the COVID-19 pandemic. The study included 8,253 children tested for suspected acute respiratory infection between January 2018 and June 2023. RSV positivity was 1.5% pre-pandemic, 1.2% during restrictions, and 5.8% post-restriction, with higher odds post-restriction. Adenovirus positivity decreased from 8.8% to 5.0% during the same periods. The authors concluded that these changes may reflect shifts in public health measures, testing practices, and healthcare-seeking behavior, rather than direct causal effects. The study provides insights into the impact of pandemic-related interventions on viral positivity rates but is limited by its unadjusted analysis and potential confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查与 COVID-19 大流行相关的三个不同时期儿童中 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和腺病毒的阳性率如何随时间变化,从而满足了解公共卫生措施对这些病毒感染的影响的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 单中心回顾性队列研究研究分三个时期进行:大流行前(2018年1月至2020年2月)、限制性大流行(2020年3月至2021年5月)和限制后(2021年6月至2023年6月)。其中包括 8,253 名 0-18 岁儿童,他们因疑似急性呼吸道感染而同时接受了 RSV 和腺病毒抗原检测。
elements_zh.methods: 未调整的比值比 (OR) 是根据特定时期的计数计算的,以大流行前时期为参考。按时期比较阳性比例,以大流行前时期作为分析基线。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,RSV 和腺病毒阳性率遵循不同的时间模式,与大流行前相比,RSV 阳性率在限制后显着增加,而腺病毒阳性率则有所下降。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,公共卫生措施和就医行为的变化可能影响了 RSV 阳性率,这可以为未来的 监测 和儿科呼吸道感染干预策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖于未经调整的比值比和潜在的混杂因素,例如季节性和测试实践。证据是中等的,因为它基于单中心回顾性分析,没有控制这些变量。

abstract_zh: 目的:描述在三个与COVID-19相关的时期中,对接受检测的儿童中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和腺病毒阳性率的时间变化。方法:本单中心回顾性队列研究研究纳入了8,253名0–18岁儿童,这些儿童在2018年1月至2023年6月期间因疑似急性呼吸道感染接受了RSV和腺病毒抗原的同步检测。时期划分为疫情前(2018年1月–2020年2月)、限制性疫情期间(2020年3月–2021年5月)和限制后(2021年6月–2023年6月)。比较各时期的阳性比例。使用疫情前时期作为参考,依据各时期计数计算未调整的比值比(OR)。结果:检测到RSV的儿童为266例(3.2%),腺病毒为612例(7.4%)。RSV阳性率在疫情前为1.5%(55/3,785),限制期间为1.2%(13/1,055),限制后为5.8%(198/3,413)。相对于疫情前时期,限制期间RSV阳性率的OR为0.85(95% CI 0.46–1.55),无显著差异;限制后OR为4.18(95% CI 3.09–5.65),显著升高。腺病毒阳性率分别为8.8%、10.2%和5.0%;对应的OR分别为1.18(95% CI 0.94–1.48)和0.54(95% CI 0.45–0.66)。结论:在临床选择的检测儿童中,RSV和腺病毒阳性率呈现不同的时间模式。这些未调整的关联不应解释为特定公共卫生措施的因果效应,因为季节性、检测实践和就医行为可能在各时期存在差异。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查与 COVID-19 大流行相关的三个不同时期儿童中 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和腺病毒的阳性率如何随时间变化,从而满足了解公共卫生措施对这些病毒感染的影响的需要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 单中心回顾性队列研究研究分三个时期进行:大流行前(2018年1月至2020年2月)、限制性大流行(2020年3月至2021年5月)和限制后(2021年6月至2023年6月)。其中包括 8,253 名 0-18 岁儿童,他们因疑似急性呼吸道感染而同时接受了 RSV 和腺病毒抗原检测。
analysis_zh.methods: 未调整的比值比 (OR) 是根据特定时期的计数计算的,以大流行前时期为参考。按时期比较阳性比例,以大流行前时期作为分析基线。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,RSV 和腺病毒阳性率遵循不同的时间模式,与大流行前相比,RSV 阳性率在限制后显着增加,而腺病毒阳性率则有所下降。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,公共卫生措施和就医行为的变化可能影响了 RSV 阳性率,这可以为未来的 监测 和儿科呼吸道感染干预策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖于未经调整的比值比和潜在的混杂因素,例如季节性和测试实践。证据是中等的,因为它基于单中心回顾性分析,没有控制这些变量。

title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Technical Report
abstract: This technical report accompanies the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) policy statement (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079047) and recommendations for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization during the 2026–2027 RSV season. The rationale is presented for recommending immunization of all infants younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of the pregnant parent; and infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. The report synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology, disease burden, immunization effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness in pediatric populations; including evidence supporting expansion of high-risk groups for second season administration. Additionally, the report provides an overview of available RSV immunization products, formulations, and coadministration with other immunizations.

title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Policy Statement
abstract: This policy statement updates recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) for the use of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization for the prevention of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) caused by RSV in infants and children. The AAP recommends RSV immunization for all infants under 8 months of age born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of their pregnant parent; and for infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. A review of evidence supports expanding the high-risk criteria for administration of RSV immunization in infants and children 8 through 19 months of age entering their second RSV season. A discussion of the evidence supporting the AAP recommendations and additional details on infants and children included in the expanded recommendations are in the accompanying technical report (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079049).

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

title: Impact of Universal Nirsevimab Immunoprophylaxis on Bronchiolitis Hospitalizations and Disease Severity in Neonates: A Real-World Single-Centre Study
abstract: (1) Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of neonatal lower respiratory tract infection. We described changes in neonatal bronchiolitis hospitalizations, RSV detection and disease severity across the transition from two seasons without systematic RSV prophylaxis to two seasons following the introduction of universal nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis (Lazio region, December 2024) in a tertiary pediatric center. (2) Methods: A retrospective, observational study was conducted at “Bambino Gesù” Children’s Hospital IRCCS (Rome, Italy) comparing four consecutive RSV seasons: pre-universal prophylaxis (2022–2024, n = 256) versus post-universal prophylaxis (2024–2026, n = 122). Term infants ≤30 days and preterm infants under term-corrected age hospitalized for acute bronchiolitis were included. RSV status was confirmed by viral testing within 72 h of admission. (3) Results: Total bronchiolitis admissions dropped by 52% (256 to 122), with RSV-positive cases decreasing from 66.8% to 43.4% (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.52–0.81; p < 0.001). Monthly peak RSV admissions fell progressively from 56 (December 2022) to 6 (January 2026). Among all admissions, ICU rates dropped from 18.4% to 4.1% (RR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.55; p < 0.001). Within RSV-positive neonates, respiratory support requirements decreased from 93.0% to 71.7% (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.65–0.92; p < 0.001), and ICU admissions declined from 24.0% to 5.7% (RR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08–0.73; p = 0.003). Non-RSV pathogens dominated the post-campaign viral profile, with the relative prevalence of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) increasing from 3.9% to 11.5% (RR 2.94, 95% CI 1.34–6.42; p = 0.006) without increasing overall severity. In the post-campaign period, 22 of 53 RSV-positive admissions occurred in nirsevimab-immunized neonates (breakthrough infections): 7/35 in 2024–25 and 15/18 in 2025–26 (p < 0.001), reflecting higher population coverage. (4) Conclusions: Universal nirsevimab prophylaxis was associated with marked reductions in neonatal bronchiolitis hospitalizations, RSV positivity, respiratory support needs, and ICU admissions. Early, high-coverage implementation prior to seasonal RSV peaks maximizes population-level protection in highly vulnerable newborns.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 普遍的 尼塞韦单抗 预防与新生儿 毛细支气管炎 住院率、RSV 阳性率、呼吸支持需求和 ICU 入院率的显着减少相关,凸显了在季节性 RSV 高峰之前早期、高覆盖率实施的有效性。

title: Hospital-based surveillance of vaccine-preventable diseases in children: a retrospective study in a Dutch tertiary hospital (2024-2025).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) are a major cause of morbidity in children, despite established immunization programs. Surveillance of VPDs is essential to inform public health strategies and strengthen national immunization programs. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of using routinely collected hospital data for in-hospital surveillance of pediatric VPDs. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in the Netherlands from July 2024 to June 2025, before national implementation of RSV immunization. Children <18 years admitted with laboratory-confirmed infections caused by pathogens with available licensed vaccines were included, regardless of inclusion in the national immunization program. Feasibility was assessed based on case ascertainment, completeness of key variables and availability of vaccination information. RESULTS: We included 99 children (103 VPD episodes; median age 0.6 years), of whom 60% (n = 59) required pediatric intensive care. Most hospitalizations were caused by respiratory infections, particularly RSV (n = 52) and influenza (n = 27). Case ascertainment required integration of multiple data sources, as 45% of children were tested outside the study hospital. Clinical variables were largely complete and vaccination status could be determined for 84% of episodes. Overall, 9% (n = 9) of VPD episodes occurred in fully vaccinated children. Most VPD episodes (76%; n = 78) occurred in children not vaccinated against the specific pathogen, mainly because they were too young or because the pathogen or serotype was not covered by the national immunization program or current guidelines. CONCLUSIONS: Retrospective hospital-based surveillance of pediatric VPDs is feasible and provides key information to guide efforts to optimize the national immunization program. By capturing disease severity and vaccine preventability, it complements existing surveillance data in the Netherlands.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估使用常规收集的医院数据进行儿科 疫苗 可预防疾病 (VPD) 住院 疫苗 的可行性,满足为公共卫生战略提供信息和加强国家免疫规划的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性 队列研究 研究于 2024 年 7 月至 2025 年 6 月在荷兰一家三级医院进行,重点关注由可获得许可的 疫苗 病原体引起的实验室确诊感染的 18 岁以下儿童,无论其是否纳入国家免疫计划。
elements_zh.methods: 根据案例确定、关键变量的完整性以及 疫苗接种 信息的可用性来评估可行性,需要集成多个数据源。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究包括 99 名儿童(103 次 VPD 发作;中位年龄 0.6 岁),其中 60% (n = 59) 需要儿科重症监护。大多数住院治疗是由呼吸道感染引起的,特别是呼吸道合胞病毒 (n = 52) 和流感 (n = 27)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于医院的儿科 VPD 回顾性 监测 是可行的,并提供了指导优化国家免疫规划工作的关键信息,补充了荷兰现有的 监测 数据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过捕获疾病的严重程度和 疫苗 的可预防性,该研究强调了整合 疫苗 医院数据的重要性,这可以为公共卫生策略提供信息并改善免疫计划。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括需要整合多个来源的数据,以及 9% 的 VPD 发作发生在完全接种疫苗的儿童中,这表明 疫苗 覆盖范围或有效性存在潜在差距。

abstract_zh: 背景:尽管制定了免疫计划,但 疫苗 可预防疾病 (VPD) 仍然是儿童发病的主要原因。VPD 的 监测 对于公共卫生战略和加强国家免疫规划至关重要。这项试点研究评估了使用常规收集的医院数据进行儿科 VPD 住院 监测 的可行性。方法:我们于2024年7月至2025年6月全国实施RSV免疫之前在荷兰一家三级医院进行了回顾性队列研究研究。无论是否纳入国家免疫计划,均包括因具有可用许可的 疫苗 病原体引起的实验室确诊感染的 18 岁以下儿童。根据案例确定、关键变量的完整性和 疫苗接种 信息的可用性来评估可行性。结果:我们纳入了 99 名儿童(103 次 VPD 发作;中位年龄 0.6 岁),其中 60% (n = 59) 需要儿科重症监护。大多数住院治疗是由呼吸道感染引起的,特别是呼吸道合胞病毒 (n = 52) 和流感 (n = 27)。病例确定需要整合多个数据源,因为 45% 的儿童在研究医院外接受了检测。临床变量基本完整,并且可以确定 84% 的发作的 疫苗接种 状态。总体而言,9% (n = 9) 的 VPD 发作发生在完全接种疫苗的儿童中。大多数 VPD 发作(76%;n = 78)发生在未接种特定病原体疫苗的儿童中,主要是因为他们太小,或者因为国家免疫计划或现行指南未涵盖病原体或血清型。结论:基于医院的儿童 VPD 回顾性 监测 是可行的,并为指导优化国家免疫规划工作提供了关键信息。通过捕获疾病严重程度和 疫苗 可预防性,它补充了荷兰现有的 监测 数据。

title: Neutrophils in Respiratory Viral Infection: Immunopathology and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: The respiratory tract is constantly exposed to microbes from the surrounding environment. This mucosal barrier requires precise control and response mechanisms that preserve gas exchange while maintaining barrier integrity. Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes, are key to maintaining this homeostasis. Both lung-resident and recruited neutrophils migrate to inflamed areas, where they perform effector functions such as phagocytosis, degranulation, reactive oxygen species production, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. These processes are tightly regulated, with immune cells such as alveolar macrophages helping to balance pathogen clearance and inflammation. Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophils contribute to inflammation and tissue damage beyond their antimicrobial roles. Elevated neutrophil levels and activation are associated with disease severity and poor outcomes following respiratory viral infection. In addition, respiratory viruses can hijack neutrophil functions to disrupt immune regulation and promote viral replication. Thus, neutrophil dysregulation has been proposed as a target for reducing acute disease severity and preventing lung injury. However, neutrophils exhibit both protective and pathogenic roles during infection, requiring therapeutic strategies that preserve their host defense while limiting pathological effects. This review summarizes current knowledge of neutrophil biology and their immunopathological roles in respiratory viral infections, focusing on Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). We also discuss therapeutic approaches targeting neutrophils, including preclinical and clinical studies, highlighting ongoing efforts to modulate neutrophil-driven inflammation.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the role of neutrophils in respiratory viral infections, particularly Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), with an emphasis on their immunopathological functions and therapeutic targeting potential.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive summary of current knowledge on neutrophil biology and their roles in respiratory viral infections, including RSV, Influenza A virus (IAV), and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). It includes preclinical and clinical studies on therapeutic approaches targeting neutrophils.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Neutrophils are critical in maintaining the mucosal barrier in the respiratory tract and are involved in both protective and pathogenic roles during infection. Their dysregulation is linked to disease severity and lung injury, making them a potential therapeutic target.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is ongoing debate about the dual roles of neutrophils in respiratory viral infections, with some evidence suggesting they contribute to inflammation and tissue damage beyond their antimicrobial functions. The review highlights the need for more research to clarify these mechanisms and develop targeted therapies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on understanding the precise mechanisms by which neutrophils contribute to both host defense and pathological outcomes in RSV infections. Therapeutic strategies should aim to modulate neutrophil-driven inflammation without compromising their protective functions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the immunopathological roles of neutrophils in respiratory viral infections, with a focus on Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). It highlights the dual functions of neutrophils in both protecting the host and contributing to inflammation and tissue damage. The review emphasizes the need for targeted therapeutic strategies that balance their protective and pathogenic effects. It also discusses the importance of further research to clarify the mechanisms underlying neutrophil dysregulation in RSV infections and to develop effective interventions.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述全面总结了当前中性粒细胞生物学知识及其在呼吸道病毒感染中的作用,包括 RSV、甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 和严重急性呼吸系统综合症冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2)。它包括针对中性粒细胞的治疗方法的临床前和临床研究。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应侧重于了解中性粒细胞在 RSV 感染中促进 宿主 防御和病理结果的精确机制。治疗策略应旨在调节中性粒细胞驱动的炎症而不损害其保护功能。

title_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染中的中性粒细胞:免疫病理学和治疗策略。
source_body_en: The respiratory tract is constantly exposed to microbes from the surrounding environment. This mucosal barrier requires precise control and response mechanisms that preserve gas exchange while maintaining barrier integrity. Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes, are key to maintaining this homeostasis. Both lung-resident and recruited neutrophils migrate to inflamed areas, where they perform effector functions such as phagocytosis, degranulation, reactive oxygen species production, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. These processes are tightly regulated, with immune cells such as alveolar macrophages helping to balance pathogen clearance and inflammation. Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophils contribute to inflammation and tissue damage beyond their antimicrobial roles. Elevated neutrophil levels and activation are associated with disease severity and poor outcomes following respiratory viral infection. In addition, respiratory viruses can hijack neutrophil functions to disrupt immune regulation and promote viral replication. Thus, neutrophil dysregulation has been proposed as a target for reducing acute disease severity and preventing lung injury. However, neutrophils exhibit both protective and pathogenic roles during infection, requiring therapeutic strategies that preserve their host defense while limiting pathological effects. This review summarizes current knowledge of neutrophil biology and their immunopathological roles in respiratory viral infections, focusing on Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). We also discuss therapeutic approaches targeting neutrophils, including preclinical and clinical studies, highlighting ongoing efforts to modulate neutrophil-driven inflammation.
abstract_zh: 呼吸道不断暴露于周围环境中的微生物。这种粘膜屏障需要精确的控制和响应机制,以保持气体交换,同时保持屏障完整性。中性粒细胞是最丰富的白细胞,是维持这种稳态的关键。肺驻留和招募的中性粒细胞都会迁移到发炎区域,在那里它们执行效应功能,例如吞噬作用、脱粒、活性氧产生和中性粒细胞胞外陷阱(NET)形成。这些过程受到严格调节,肺泡巨噬细胞等免疫细胞有助于平衡病原体清除和炎症。新的证据表明,中性粒细胞除了发挥抗菌作用外,还会导致炎症和组织损伤。中性粒细胞水平和激活升高与呼吸道病毒感染后疾病的严重程度和不良结果相关。此外,呼吸道病毒可以劫持中性粒细胞功能,破坏免疫调节并促进病毒复制。因此,中性粒细胞失调已被提议作为降低急性疾病严重程度和预防肺损伤的目标。然而,中性粒细胞在感染过程中同时表现出保护性和致病性作用,需要在限制病理效应的同时保留其 宿主 防御的治疗策略。本综述总结了中性粒细胞生物学的最新知识及其在呼吸道病毒感染中的免疫病理学作用,重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2)、甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)。我们还讨论了针对中性粒细胞的治疗方法,包括临床前和临床研究,强调了调节中性粒细胞驱动的炎症的持续努力。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述全面总结了当前中性粒细胞生物学知识及其在呼吸道病毒感染中的作用,包括 RSV、甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 和严重急性呼吸系统综合症冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2)。它包括针对中性粒细胞的治疗方法的临床前和临床研究。

title: Comprehensive Performance Verification of the Mindray MN2880 System in Detecting Respiratory Virus Nucleic Acids.
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To verify the clinical performance of the Mindray MN2880 system for simultaneous detection of SARS‐CoV‐2, influenza A virus (IAV), influenza B virus (IBV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) nucleic acids. Methods According to the CNAS‐GL039:2019 and CNAS‐GL037:2019 requirements for molecular diagnostic verification, we comprehensively evaluated the Mindray MN2880 multiplex respiratory virus assay across seven critical performance parameters: clinical concordance, limit of detection (LoD), repeatability, precision, cross‐reactivity/interference resistance, daily QC, and contamination control. Results The Mindray MN2880 system demonstrated high diagnostic concordance with the reference method, with total percent agreements of 99.51% (95% CI: 99.00%–99.76%) for SARS‐CoV‐2, 99.93% (95% CI: 99.60%–99.99%) for IAV, and 100% for both IBV and RSV, and achieved clinically verified limits of detection (LoD: SARS‐CoV‐2 at 100 copies/mL, IAV/IBV/RSV at 200 copies/mL). Analytical precision was confirmed through 100% detection across negative/low/medium/high concentration panels with ≤ 3% CV for repeatability (Ct values) and ≤ 5% CV for inter‐run precision. The assay exhibited 100% specificity against 6 clinically relevant pathogens, including Human Rhinovirus, parainfluenza virus, adenovirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , Haemophilus influenzae , and Staphylococcus aureus , with no observed cross‐reactivity. Moreover, the MN2880 system demonstrated robust interference resistance (100% detection of weakly‐positive samples spiked with seven interferents), stable daily QC performance (100% valid controls across 115 consecutive runs), and 100% contamination prevention. Conclusion The MN2880 system satisfies key analytical benchmarks required for diagnostic use in respiratory virus multiplex testing, with performance verified against CNAS‐GL039:2019 and CNAS‐GL037:2019 standards.
