source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To verify the clinical performance of the Mindray MN2880 system for simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus (IAV), influenza B virus (IBV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) nucleic acids. METHODS: According to the CNAS-GL039:2019 and CNAS-GL037:2019 requirements for molecular diagnostic verification, we comprehensively evaluated the Mindray MN2880 multiplex respiratory virus assay across seven critical performance parameters: clinical concordance, limit of detection (LoD), repeatability, precision, cross-reactivity/interference resistance, daily QC, and contamination control. RESULTS: The Mindray MN2880 system demonstrated high diagnostic concordance with the reference method, with total percent agreements of 99.51% (95% CI: 99.00%-99.76%) for SARS-CoV-2, 99.93% (95% CI: 99.60%-99.99%) for IAV, and 100% for both IBV and RSV, and achieved clinically verified limits of detection (LoD: SARS-CoV-2 at 100 copies/mL, IAV/IBV/RSV at 200 copies/mL). Analytical precision was confirmed through 100% detection across negative/low/medium/high concentration panels with ≤ 3% CV for repeatability (Ct values) and ≤ 5% CV for inter-run precision. The assay exhibited 100% specificity against 6 clinically relevant pathogens, including Human Rhinovirus, parainfluenza virus, adenovirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Staphylococcus aureus, with no observed cross-reactivity. Moreover, the MN2880 system demonstrated robust interference resistance (100% detection of weakly-positive samples spiked with seven interferents), stable daily QC performance (100% valid controls across 115 consecutive runs), and 100% contamination prevention. CONCLUSION: The MN2880 system satisfies key analytical benchmarks required for diagnostic use in respiratory virus multiplex testing, with performance verified against CNAS-GL039:2019 and CNAS-GL037:2019 standards.

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的验证迈瑞 MN2880 系统同时检测 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感病毒(IAV)、乙型流感病毒(IBV)和 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)核酸的临床性能。方法 根据 CNAS-GL039:2019 和 CNAS-GL037:2019 分子诊断验证要求,我们对迈瑞 MN2880 多重呼吸道病毒检测的七个关键性能参数进行了全面评估:临床一致性、检测限 (LoD)、重复性、精密度、交叉反应/抗干扰性、日常质量控制和污染控制。结果迈瑞 MN2880 系统与参考方法表现出高度的诊断一致性,SARS-CoV-2 的总一致性百分比为 99.51%(95% CI:99.00%–99.76%),IAV 的总一致性百分比为 99.93%(95% CI:99.60%–99.99%),IBV 和 RSV 的总一致性百分比均为 100%,并达到了临床验证的极限检测范围(LoD:SARS-CoV-2 为 100 拷贝/mL,IAV/IBV/RSV 为 200 拷贝/mL)。通过阴性/低/中/高浓度组的 100% 检测来确认分析精度,重复性(Ct 值)的 CV ≤ 3%,批间精度的 CV ≤ 5%。该检测对 6 种临床相关病原体表现出 100% 特异性,包括人鼻病毒、副流感病毒、腺病毒、肺炎支原体、流感嗜血杆菌和金黄色葡萄球菌,未观察到交叉反应。此外,MN2880 系统表现出强大的抗干扰性(100% 检测出掺有 7 种干扰物的弱阳性样品)、稳定的日常 QC 性能(115 次连续运行中 100% 有效对照)以及 100% 污染预防。结论 MN2880 系统满足呼吸道病毒多重检测诊断用途所需的关键分析基准,其性能已根据 CNAS-GL039:2019 和 CNAS-GL037:2019 标准进行了验证。

title: Antiviral Drug Development against RNA Viruses: Progress, Clinical Translation and Persistent Challenges
abstract: Antiviral drug development has produced transformative treatments for some RNA-virus infections while leaving major gaps in acute respiratory, haemorrhagic and enteric disease. The unevenness of progress cannot be explained by target availability alone. This critical narrative review examines how viral biology, pharmacological exposure, disease timing, trial design, resistance and health-system access jointly determine whether an antiviral candidate becomes a clinically useful intervention. Peer-reviewed mechanistic studies, randomised trials, methodological papers and authoritative institutional evidence published from 2000 to 13 August 2026 were critically synthesised, with earlier foundational findings considered where necessary. Durable combination treatment for human immunodeficiency virus and curative direct-acting treatment for hepatitis C show what sustained target validation and clinical development can achieve. Conversely, trials of influenza, coronavirus disease 2019, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue and emerging infections demonstrate the difficulty of translating reductions in viral replication into reliable effects on symptoms, hospitalisation, transmission or survival. Contrasting remdesivir outcomes across disease stages, context-dependent results for oral coronavirus antivirals, a promising but geographically limited paediatric respiratory syncytial virus trial, and dengue human-challenge studies illustrate why positive virological or early clinical findings require precise interpretation. Resistance is shaped by drug mechanism, treatment exposure, viral population dynamics and surveillance quality, rather than by a uniform property of all RNA viruses. Apparent broad-spectrum activity may also reflect assay artefacts or non-physiological experimental systems. Priorities include pharmacologically credible discovery platforms, earlier diagnosis and treatment, adaptive trials with prespecified patient-important endpoints, resistance-informed combinations, outbreak-ready trial infrastructure and affordability planned before licensing. The central conclusion is that antiviral innovation is most effective when molecular specificity, clinically relevant timing and equitable implementation are developed as a connected evidence pathway.

abstract_zh: 抗病毒药物 药物开发已经产生了针对某些 RNA 病毒感染的革命性 治疗,同时在急性呼吸道、出血和肠道疾病方面留下了重大空白。进展的不平衡不能仅用目标的可用性来解释。这篇批判性的叙述性综述探讨了病毒生物学、药理学暴露、疾病时机、试验设计、耐药性和卫生系统准入如何共同决定 抗病毒药物 候选药物是否成为临床上有用的干预措施。严格综合了 2000 年至 2026 年 8 月 13 日发表的同行评审机制研究、随机试验、方法论论文和权威机构证据,并在必要时考虑了早期的基础研究结果。针对人类免疫缺陷病毒的持久组合 治疗 和针对丙型肝炎的治疗性直接作用 治疗 显示了持续的靶标验证和临床开发可以实现的目标。相反,流感、2019冠状病毒病、呼吸道合胞病毒、登革热和新出现的感染的试验表明,将病毒复制的减少转化为对症状、住院、呼吸道合胞病毒或生存的可靠影响是困难的。不同疾病阶段的瑞德西韦结果对比、口腔冠状病毒 抗病毒药物 的背景依赖性结果、一项有前景但地理上有限的儿科 呼吸道合胞病毒 试验以及登革热人类挑战研究说明了为什么阳性病毒学或早期临床发现需要精确解释。耐药性是由药物机制、治疗 暴露、病毒群体动态和 监测 质量决定的,而不是由所有 RNA 病毒的统一特性决定的。表观的广谱活性也可能反映测定假象或非生理实验系统。优先事项包括药理学上可信的发现平台、早期的 诊断 和 治疗、预先指定的患者重要终点的适应性试验、耐药性信息组合、暴发 就绪的试验基础设施以及许可前计划的可负担性。中心结论是,当分子特异性、临床相关时机和公平实施被开发为相互关联的证据途径时,抗病毒药物 创新是最有效的。

title: [Chinese guidelines for the diagnosis and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (2026 revision)].
abstract: The Chinese guidelines for the diagnosis and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (2026 revision) were developed by the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Groups of the Chinese Thoracic Society and the Chinese Association of Chest Physicians. Building on the 2021 edition, this revision incorporates evidence published over the past five years and experience from COPD prevention and management in China, and provides comprehensive updates on disease definition, etiology and pathogenesis, case finding, diagnosis and comprehensive assessment, stable COPD management, diagnosis and treatment of acute exacerbations, comorbidity management, and future research directions. The guideline primarily applies the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, supplemented by the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence, to assess the certainty of evidence and develop recommendations. It offers practical recommendations for the diagnosis and management of COPD across 22 clinical questions. It aims to promote early identification, standardized diagnosis and treatment, and comprehensive management of COPD, and therefore to improve the standardized care and reduce the disease burden of COPD in China.The 22 key clinical questions and corresponding recommendations are summarized as follows.Question 1: Given the current underdiagnosis of COPD, which strategies can improve early diagnosis?Recommendation 1: We recommend active and opportunistic case finding to identify individuals at high risk of COPD and facilitate early diagnosis. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 2: Which parameters should be assessed when selecting initial pharmacotherapy for patients with COPD?Recommendation 2: Patients with COPD should undergo individualized assessment based on symptom burden and exacerbation risk and be classified into groups A, B, or E. Additional assessments should include the severity of airflow obstruction on pulmonary function testing, comorbidities, and biomarkers such as the peripheral blood eosinophil count. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 3: How should the mMRC and CAT scores be used for symptom assessment in the ABE classification?Recommendation 3: Symptoms of COPD should be assessed using the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale and/or the COPD Assessment Test (CAT). Results from the two instruments may be discordant: the mMRC scale focuses on dyspnea, whereas the CAT is more suitable for a comprehensive assessment of multiple symptoms. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 4: Should chest CT be included in the initial assessment of COPD?Recommendation 4: Chest imaging should be included in the initial assessment of COPD, with chest computed tomography (CT) preferred. (2B/conditional recommendation)Question 5: What are the key preventive measures targeting exposure to risk factors?Recommendation 5: Smoking cessation interventions should be actively provided to all patients with COPD. Clean fuels, effective ventilation, nonpolluting stoves, and similar measures are recommended to reduce harmful environmental exposures; occupational protection should also be strengthened to avoid continued exposure to potential irritants. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 6: How should vaccination be recommended for patients with COPD?Recommendation 6: Annual influenza vaccination is recommended. Regular pneumococcal vaccination with PPSV23 is also recommended, with PCV20 or PCV21 as options for susceptible individuals; the specific pneumococcal vaccination schedule should follow product-specific prescribing information. (1A/strong recommendation). Vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap), and herpes zoster is suggested. (1A/conditional recommendation)Question 7: How should initial pharmacotherapy be selected according to the ABE classification and the peripheral blood eosinophil count?Recommendation 7: Initial pharmacotherapy should be selected according to symptoms, exacerbation risk, and the peripheral blood eosinophil count. For patients in group E, regimens that reduce the risk of future exacerbations should be prioritized. When the peripheral blood eosinophil count is ≥300 cells/μl, triple inhaled therapy[inhaled corticosteroids(ICS) plus long-acting β2 agonists (LABA) plus long-acting muscarinic antagonists(LAMA)] is recommended to achieve a state of low disease activity characterized by freedom from exacerbations. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 8: What are the indications for adding an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy?Recommendation 8: The addition of an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy is recommended for patients with COPD who have any of the following features: (1)≥1 moderate or severe COPD exacerbation per year; (2) a blood eosinophil count ≥300 cells/μl, or ≥100 cells/μl during follow-up assessment; or (3) a history of asthma or concomitant asthma-like features. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 9: How should a standardized pathway for follow-up assessment and pharmacological treatment adjustment be established for patients with stable COPD?Recommendation 9: During follow-up pharmacotherapy, treatment adjustment should be guided by two core treatable traits: persistent dyspnea and the occurrence of exacerbations. For patients with persistently poor symptom control, bronchodilator therapy should be optimized stepwise after inhaler technique, adherence, and the effects of comorbidities have been assessed. For patients who continue to experience exacerbations, the addition, continuation, or cautious withdrawal of ICS should be guided by the current regimen and peripheral blood eosinophil count. Biologic therapy is appropriate for selected high-risk populations. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 10: How should treatment be optimized and adjusted for patients already receiving ICS+LABA therapy?Recommendation 10: Patients receiving ICS+LABA may continue the regimen if their condition is stable. If exacerbations persist, escalation to triple therapy with ICS+LABA+LAMA is recommended. For patients with COPD who are at high risk of pulmonary infection, including mycobacterial infection, withdrawal of ICS and a switch to dual bronchodilator therapy should be considered to reduce the risk of further infections. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 11: What are the indications for biologic therapy in patients with COPD?Recommendation 11: For patients who continue to experience recurrent exacerbations despite ICS+LABA+LAMA therapy, inhaled medication use, comorbidities and other contributing factors should be assessed, and biologic therapy should be selected on an individualized basis according to features such as the peripheral blood eosinophil count and the presence of chronic bronchitis. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 12: How should an inhaler device be selected according to individual patient characteristics?Recommendation 12: The most appropriate inhaler device and medication should be selected according to whether the patient has adequate inspiratory flow, hand-mouth coordination, and the ability to inhale independently, as well as the characteristics of the device and medication. Training in inhaler technique and individualized assessment should be reinforced. (4/strong recommendation)Question 13: How should pulmonary rehabilitation be implemented for patients with COPD?Recommendation 13: Dynamic pulmonary rehabilitation assessment is recommended before treatment and at different stages during treatment, including clinical, functional, nutritional, and psychological assessments. Pulmonary rehabilitation should be initiated as early as possible in patients with stable COPD who have no absolute contraindications. For patients with acute exacerbations of COPD, pulmonary rehabilitation should be provided early during hospitalization and after discharge. An individualized rehabilitation prescription should be developed according to assessment findings and may include airway clearance techniques, breathing training, aerobic and resistance exercise, positioning, and respiratory support. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 14: What are the indications and treatment regimen for oxygen therapy in stable COPD?Recommendation 14: Long-term oxygen therapy is recommended for patients with COPD and severe resting hypoxemia, defined as either (1) PaO2≤55 mmHg(1 mmHg=0.133 kPa) or SpO2≤88% at rest, or (2) PaO2 of 55-60 mmHg or SpO2 of 88%-89% at rest together with pulmonary hypertension, peripheral edema suggestive of congestive heart failure, or polycythemia (hematocrit>55%). Oxygen should be administered for at least 15 h/day to maintain PaO2 ≥60 mmHg and/or SpO2 ≥90%. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 15: What are the indications for noninvasive ventilation in stable COPD?Recommendation 15: Long-term noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is suggested for patients with severe chronic hypercapnia and a history of hospitalization for acute respiratory failure, or for those with persistent daytime hypercapnia (PaCO2>53 mmHg). (1B/strong recommendation)Question 16: Which pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions can reduce mortality in patients with COPD?Recommendation 16: Smoking cessation, pharmacotherapy (fixed-dose triple therapy), and nonpharmacological interventions, including pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term oxygen therapy, noninvasive ventilation, and surgical lung volume reduction, are recommended to reduce mortality in patients with COPD. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 17: How should bronchoscopic interventional therapies be selected for patients with COPD?Recommendation 17: Bronchoscopic interventions, including endobronchial valves and thermal vapor ablation, are recommended for selected patients with advanced emphysema and COPD. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 18: What are the indications for lung transplantation in patients with COPD?Recommendation 18: For patients with very severe COPD (progressive disease with a BODE index of 7-10 who are not candidates for lung volume reduction surgery), referral for lung transplantation may be considered if at least one of the following is present: (1) a history of hospitalization for an acute hypercapnic exacerbation (PaCO2>50 mmHg); (2) pulmonary hypertension and/or cor pulmonale despite oxygen therapy; or (3) FEV1<20% predicted together with DLCO<20% predicted or homogeneous emphysema. (3B/conditional recommendation)Question 19: How should systemic corticosteroids be used for acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 19: For moderate or severe acute exacerbations of COPD, low-dose, short-course systemic corticosteroid therapy is suggested; routine prolongation of treatment or use of high-dose systemic corticosteroids is not recommended. Nebulized budesonide may be considered as an alternative for patients with contraindications to systemic corticosteroids or a high risk of adverse reactions. (Very low-quality evidence/weak recommendation)Question 20: How should high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy be used in the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 20: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy is suggested for patients with an acute exacerbation of COPD who have persistent hypoxemia, cannot tolerate NIV or have contraindications to NIV, require sequential oxygen therapy after NIV, or require prevention of reintubation after extubation. In patients with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure who meet the indications for NIV, HFNC should not replace NIV as the preferred initial treatment. (1B/conditional recommendation)Question 21: What are the indications for noninvasive ventilation in the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 21: NIV is recommended for patients with an acute exacerbation of COPD who have any of the following: (1) respiratory acidosis (PaCO2 ≥6.0 kPa or 45 mmHg and arterial pH≤7.35); (2) severe dyspnea with clinical signs of respiratory muscle fatigue and/or increased work of breathing, such as use of accessory respiratory muscles, paradoxical thoracoabdominal motion, or intercostal retraction; (3) persistent hypoxemia despite oxygen therapy; or (4) a need for sequential invasive-noninvasive mechanical ventilation. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 22: What measures are recommended to prevent acute exacerbations of COPD?Recommendation 22: After an acute exacerbation, the management plans for COPD and its comorbidities should be evaluated, and appropriate measures should be implemented to prevent further exacerbations, particularly peri-discharge management, long-term standardized pharmacotherapy, smoking cessation, vaccination, and nonpharmacological interventions such as pulmonary rehabilitation. (4/strong recommendation).

Additional assessments should include the severity of airflow obstruction on pulmonary function testing, comorbidities, and biomarkers such as the peripheral blood eosinophil count. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 3: How should the mMRC and CAT scores be used for symptom assessment in the ABE classification?Recommendation 3: Symptoms of COPD should be assessed using the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale and/or the COPD Assessment Test (CAT). Results from the two instruments may be discordant: the mMRC scale focuses on dyspnea, whereas the CAT is more suitable for a comprehensive assessment of multiple symptoms. (2B/strong recommendation)Question 4: Should chest CT be included in the initial assessment of COPD?Recommendation 4: Chest imaging should be included in the initial assessment of COPD, with chest computed tomography (CT) preferred. (2B/conditional recommendation)Question 5: What are the key preventive measures targeting exposure to risk factors?Recommendation 5: Smoking cessation interventions should be actively provided to all patients with COPD. Clean fuels, effective ventilation, nonpolluting stoves, and similar measures are recommended to reduce harmful environmental exposures; occupational protection should also be strengthened to avoid continued exposure to potential irritants. (1A/strong recommendation)Question 6: How should vaccination be recommended for patients with COPD?Recommendation 6: Annual influenza vaccination is recommended. Regular pneumococcal vaccination with PPSV23 is also recommended, with PCV20 or PCV21 as options for susceptible individuals; the specific pneumococcal vaccination schedule should follow product-specific prescribing information. (1A/strong recommendation). Vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Tdap), and herpes zoster is suggested. (1A/conditional recommendation)Question 7: How should initial pharmacotherapy be selected according to the ABE classification and the peripheral blood eosinophil count?Recommendation 7: Initial pharmacotherapy should be selected according to symptoms, exacerbation risk, and the peripheral blood eosinophil count. For patients in group E, regimens that reduce the risk of future exacerbations should be prioritized. When the peripheral blood eosinophil count is ≥300 cells/μl, triple inhaled therapy[inhaled corticosteroids(ICS) plus long-acting β2 agonists (LABA) plus long-acting muscarinic antagonists(LAMA)] is recommended to achieve a state of low disease activity characterized by freedom from exacerbations. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 8: What are the indications for adding an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy?Recommendation 8: The addition of an ICS to long-acting bronchodilator therapy is recommended for patients with COPD who have any of the following features: (1)≥1 moderate or severe COPD exacerbation per year; (2) a blood eosinophil count ≥300 cells/μl, or ≥100 cells/μl during follow-up assessment; or (3) a history of asthma or concomitant asthma-like features. (1B/strong recommendation)Question 16: Which pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions can reduce mortality in patients with COPD?Recommendation 16: Smoking cessation, pharmacotherapy (fixed-dose triple therapy), and nonpharmacological interventions, including pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term oxygen therapy, noninvasive ventilation, and surgical lung volume reduction, are recommended to reduce mortality in patients with COPD. (4/strong recommendation).

abstract_zh: 中国慢性阻塞性肺疾病诊断及治疗指南(2026年修订)由中华医学会胸科学会慢性阻塞性肺病学组和中华医学会胸科医师分会慢性阻塞性肺病学组制定。此次修订在2021年版的基础上,结合了过去五年发表的证据和中国慢阻肺预防和管理的经验,对疾病定义、病因和发病机制、病例发现、诊断和综合评估、慢阻肺稳定管理、急性加重的诊断和诊断、合并症管理以及未来的研究方向进行了全面更新。该指南主要采用建议分级评估、制定和评估(GRADE)方法,并辅以牛津循证医学中心的证据水平,评估证据的确定性并制定建议。它为 诊断 和 COPD 的 22 个临床问题的管理提供了实用建议。旨在促进COPD的早期识别、标准化诊断和诊断以及综合管理,从而提高我国COPD的规范化护理水平,减轻COPD的疾病负担。22个关键临床问题和相应建议总结如下。问题1:鉴于目前COPD诊断不足的情况,哪些策略可以改善早期诊断?建议1:我们建议积极和机会性病例发现,以识别高危人群COPD 并促进早期 诊断。(1B/强推荐)问题2:慢阻肺患者选择初始药物治疗时应评估哪些参数?建议2:慢阻肺患者应根据症状负担和加重风险进行个体化评估,分为A、B、E组。其他评估还应包括肺功能检测中气流阻塞的严重程度、合并症以及外周血嗜酸性粒细胞计数等生物标志物。(2B/强推荐)问题3:ABE分类中应如何使用mMRC和CAT评分进行症状评估?建议3:应使用改良医学研究委员会(mMRC)呼吸困难量表和/或COPD评估测试(CAT)来评估COPD症状。两种仪器的结果可能不一致:mMRC 量表侧重于呼吸困难,而 CAT 更适合对多种症状进行综合评估。(2B/强推荐)问题4:慢性阻塞性肺疾病(COPD)的初步评估应包括胸部CT吗?建议4:慢性阻塞性肺病(COPD)的初步评估应包括胸部影像学,首选胸部计算机断层扫描(CT)。(2B/有条件推荐)问题5:针对危险因素暴露的关键预防措施有哪些?建议5:应积极向所有COPD患者提供戒烟干预措施。建议使用清洁燃料、有效通风、无污染炉灶和类似措施,以减少有害环境暴露;还应加强职业防护,避免持续接触潜在刺激物。(1A/强推荐)问题6:COPD患者应该如何推荐疫苗接种?建议6:推荐每年流感疫苗接种。还推荐常规肺炎球菌 有哮喘病史或伴有哮喘样特征。(1B/强推荐)问题9:稳定期COPD患者应如何建立标准化的随访评估和药理学治疗调整路径?建议9:随访药物治疗期间,治疗调整应以两个核心可治疗特征为指导:持续性呼吸困难和病情加重的发生。对于症状控制持续不佳的患者,应在评估吸入器技术、依从性和合并症的影响后逐步优化支气管扩张剂治疗。对于持续病情加重的患者,ICS的添加、继续或谨慎停药应以当前治疗方案和外周血嗜酸性粒细胞计数为指导。生物疗法适用于选定的高危人群。(1B/强推荐)问题10:对于已经接受ICS+LABA治疗的患者,治疗应该如何优化和调整?建议10:接受ICS+LABA治疗的患者如果病情稳定,可以继续治疗。如果病情持续恶化,建议升级至 严重呼吸困难,伴有呼吸肌疲劳和/或呼吸功增加的临床症状,例如使用辅助呼吸肌、反常的胸腹运动或肋间回缩;(3) 尽管接受氧疗,仍持续低氧血症;(4) analysis_zh.main_results: 该指南为 COPD 诊断 和管理提供了 22 条实用建议,包括病例发现、初始药物治疗、胸部 CT、预防措施和 疫苗接种 建议。

title: Nasal Mucosal Immunity is Associated with Protection against RSV Illness in Infants
abstract: Background: Despite advances in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis, RSV remains a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Immunity at the site of infection is potentially important yet airway mucosal immunity against RSV infection remains poorly defined. We collected nasal and blood samples across three pediatric cohorts: 1) children presenting to the emergency department with respiratory symptoms; 2) infants and mothers presenting to an urban hospital system across the RSV season; 3) infants born to mothers vaccinated with maternal pre-Fusion (F) vaccine. We analyzed mucosal and serologic anti-RSV antibodies and assessed for factors impacting titer magnitude and durability. Specimens from 285 infants/young children and 39 mothers were analyzed. Mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels were lower in infants presenting with RSV infection compared to age-matched controls both in infants experiencing their first viral season (p = 0.0011) and older children (p < 0.0001). Higher levels of mucosal antibodies were seen in infants whose mothers received maternal pre-F vaccination, with IgG against RSV fusion protein tightly correlating between infant serum and nasal compartments (p < 0.0001). However, mucosal anti-RSV IgG waned significantly by 6 months of age (p < 0.0001). Higher mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels are associated with protection against RSV-related illness. Current immunoprophylactic strategies drive robust anti-RSV IgG responses in the infant mucosal and serological compartments; however, passive immunity wanes over 6 months. These results suggest that RSV immunization strategies optimizing durable mucosal immunity may protect infants from RSV-related respiratory illness.

title_zh: 鼻粘膜免疫与婴儿 RSV 疾病的预防相关
source_body_en: Background: Despite advances in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis, RSV remains a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Immunity at the site of infection is potentially important yet airway mucosal immunity against RSV infection remains poorly defined. We collected nasal and blood samples across three pediatric cohorts: 1) children presenting to the emergency department with respiratory symptoms; 2) infants and mothers presenting to an urban hospital system across the RSV season; 3) infants born to mothers vaccinated with maternal pre-Fusion (F) vaccine. We analyzed mucosal and serologic anti-RSV antibodies and assessed for factors impacting titer magnitude and durability. Specimens from 285 infants/young children and 39 mothers were analyzed. Mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels were lower in infants presenting with RSV infection compared to age-matched controls both in infants experiencing their first viral season (p = 0.0011) and older children (p < 0.0001). Higher levels of mucosal antibodies were seen in infants whose mothers received maternal pre-F vaccination, with IgG against RSV fusion protein tightly correlating between infant serum and nasal compartments (p < 0.0001). However, mucosal anti-RSV IgG waned significantly by 6 months of age (p < 0.0001). Higher mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels are associated with protection against RSV-related illness. Current immunoprophylactic strategies drive robust anti-RSV IgG responses in the infant mucosal and serological compartments; however, passive immunity wanes over 6 months. These results suggest that RSV immunization strategies optimizing durable mucosal immunity may protect infants from RSV-related respiratory illness.
abstract_zh: 背景:尽管 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 免疫预防取得了进展,RSV 仍然是婴儿严重呼吸道疾病的主要原因。感染部位的免疫力可能很重要,但针对 RSV 感染的气道粘膜免疫力仍然不明确。我们收集了三名儿科 队列研究 的鼻腔和血液样本:1) 因呼吸道症状而到急诊室就诊的儿童;2) 在 RSV 季节期间到城市医院系统就诊的婴儿和母亲;3) 接种母体预融合 (F) 疫苗 的母亲所生的婴儿。我们分析了粘膜和血清学抗 RSV 抗体,并评估了影响滴度大小和持久性的因素。对 285 名婴儿/幼儿和 39 名母亲的样本进行了分析。与年龄匹配的对照组相比,在经历第一个病毒季节的婴儿 (p = 0.0011) 和年龄较大的儿童 (p < 0.0001) 中,出现 RSV 感染的婴儿的粘膜抗 RSV 抗体水平较低。在母亲接受母体 pre-F 疫苗接种 的婴儿中观察到较高水平的粘膜抗体,针对 RSV 融合蛋白的 IgG 在婴儿血清和鼻腔室之间紧密相关 (p < 0.0001)。然而,到 6 个月大时,粘膜抗 RSV IgG 显着减弱 (p < 0.0001)。较高的粘膜抗 RSV 抗体水平与预防 RSV 相关疾病有关。当前的免疫预防策略在婴儿粘膜和血清学区室中驱动强大的抗 RSV IgG 反应;然而,被动免疫力在 6 个月内减弱。这些结果表明,优化持久粘膜免疫的 RSV 免疫策略可以保护婴儿免受 RSV 相关呼吸道疾病的侵害。

title: Data-driven forecasting of Flu, RSV, and COVID-19 related outcomes in the United States and Canada via Hankel dynamic mode decomposition.
abstract: The (large) season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history make the forecasting of infectious diseases a challenging problem. Here, we examine the extent to which advances in data-driven dynamical modeling can provide accurate predictions by benchmarking the performance of one such method, Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), on the 2024-2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada. Using Hankel-DMD, we generated weekly forecasts that were submitted to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph's AI4CastingHub. Across both Hubs, we find that Hankel-DMD can provide high quality forecasts at the beginning and end of the season, but forecasts in the middle of the season suffer from significant overestimation of the season peak. This leads to worse than baseline performance on FluSight Forecast Hub, when submissions are evaluated across the entire season. Hankel-DMD is found to be the best among a small number of models that submitted enough forecasts against which to compare for forecasting influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 in Canada. As this was the first active year of AI4CastingHub, this suggests that Hankel-DMD may be especially useful when expertise is lacking for predicting infectious dynamics in new regions. To study how Hankel-DMD can be better equipped to provide accurate forecasts during the season peak, we explored whether DMD with memory, a recently developed approach for applying DMD to non-stationary dynamical systems, provides significant improvements. Retrospective analysis using DMD with memory shows promise in reducing overestimation during season peak, but the extent to which its optimal use can be achieved in a live forecasting setting remains to be seen. Collectively, our results demonstrate that Hankel-DMD has potential as an efficient and interpretable method for the forecasting of infectious diseases, while also highlighting a number of remaining methodological challenges which future work should aim to address.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the potential of data-driven dynamical modeling, specifically Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), for forecasting infectious disease outcomes, addressing the challenge posed by season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a retrospective analysis of the 2024-2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada, comparing forecasts generated using Hankel-DMD against those submitted to the CDC's FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph's AI4CastingHub.
analysis.methods: Hankel-DMD was used to generate weekly forecasts, which were submitted to the FluSight Forecast Hub and AI4CastingHub for evaluation. The method was benchmarked against other models that submitted forecasts for the same seasons.
analysis.main_results: Hankel-DMD provided high-quality forecasts at the beginning and end of the season but significantly overestimated the peak during the middle of the season. This overestimation led to worse than baseline performance on the FluSight Forecast Hub.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that while Hankel-DMD is a promising method for forecasting infectious diseases, its performance during the season peak requires further refinement. The study highlights the potential of this method as well as its current limitations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that Hankel-DMD could be a valuable tool for forecasting respiratory syncytial virus and other infectious diseases, aiding in public health planning and resource allocation, particularly in regions with limited expertise.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective nature and the limited number of models used for comparison may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate, as the performance was evaluated across the entire season, and the method's effectiveness during the peak remains uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) in forecasting respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other infectious disease outcomes in the United States and Canada. The research highlights the challenges of forecasting due to season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history. Using a data-driven approach, the study generated weekly forecasts for the 2024-2025 seasons and submitted them to the CDC's FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph's AI4CastingHub. The results show that Hankel-DMD provides high-quality forecasts at the start and end of the season but overestimates the peak during the middle, leading to worse than baseline performance. The study suggests that while Hankel-DMD has potential as an efficient and interpretable forecasting method, its performance during the peak of the season requires further improvement. The findings are significant for public health planning but are limited by the retrospective nature of the analysis and the small number of models used for comparison. The evidence is moderate, as the performance was evaluated across the entire season, and the method's effectiveness during the peak remains uncertain.

abstract_zh: (大的)季节变化和有限的动态历史使得传染病的预测成为一个具有挑战性的问题。在这里,我们通过对一种方法 Hankel 动态模式分解 (DMD) 对美国和加拿大 2024-2025 年流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 COVID-19 季节的性能进行基准测试,研究数据驱动的动态建模的进步在多大程度上可以提供准确的预测。使用 Hankel-DMD,我们生成了每周预测,并提交给疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 的 FluSight 预测中心和圭尔夫大学的 AI4CastingHub。在这两个中心,我们发现 Hankel-DMD 可以在季节开始和结束时提供高质量的预测,但季节中期的预测严重高估了季节高峰。当对整个季节的提交进行评估时,这会导致 FluSight Forecast Hub 的基准性能更差。Hankel-DMD 被认为是少数模型中最好的,这些模型提交了足够的预测,可以与加拿大的流感、RSV 和 COVID-19 的预测进行比较。由于这是 AI4CastingHub 的第一个活跃年份,这表明当缺乏预测新地区感染动态的专业知识时,Hankel-DMD 可能特别有用。为了研究 Hankel-DMD 如何更好地在季节高峰期间提供准确的预测,我们探讨了带记忆的 DMD(一种最近开发的将 DMD 应用于非平稳动力系统的方法)是否能提供显着的改进。使用具有记忆功能的 DMD 进行回顾性分析显示,有望减少季节高峰期间的高估,但在实时预测环境中其最佳使用程度仍有待观察。总的来说,我们的结果表明 Hankel-DMD 具有作为一种有效且可解释的传染病预测方法的潜力,同时也强调了未来工作应致力于解决的许多剩余方法学挑战。

title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). METHODS: Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. RESULTS: We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. CONCLUSION: Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.

title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title_zh: 从实验室定量到快速现场测试:针对 RSV F 蛋白的高亲和力单克隆抗体对的筛选以及跨多个检测平台的分析评估。
source_body_en: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.
abstract_zh: 针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) F 蛋白的单克隆抗体是基于抗原的 诊断 的关键试剂,但与多种检测格式兼容的抗体对仍然有限。在这项研究中,用重组后RSV F蛋白免疫BALB/c小鼠,产生六种分泌抗RSV F单克隆抗体的杂交瘤细胞系。通过间接 ELISA、Western blotting 和表面等离子共振对抗体进行表征,并通过交叉配对 ELISA 选择最佳夹心对。mAb-14/mAb-26对表现出高亲和力和最佳配对性能,用于建立双抗体夹心ELISA(DAS-ELISA)、基于磁性微粒的化学发光免疫分析和基于Au@Pt纳米颗粒的侧流免疫分析(Au@Pt-LFIA)。检测限分别为 0.25、0.04 和 0.78 ng/mL。Au@Pt-LFIA 的视觉检测限比传统胶体金免疫层析低约四倍,无需额外的信号放大步骤。三种方法均未显示出与七种测试的异源呼吸道病原体抗原的可检测的交叉反应性。初步临床样本检测中,DAS-ELISA、化学发光免疫分析和Au@Pt-LFIA的阳性一致性百分比分别为90.0%、93.3%和83.3%,所有方法的阴性一致性百分比均为100.0%。这些结果支持 mAb-14/mAb-26 作为通用抗体对,用于跨互补实验室和现场检测平台检测 RSV 抗原。

title: Dual-aptamer magnetic capture and electrochemical detection of influenza B and respiratory syncytial viruses in artificial saliva.
abstract: Saliva is a promising non-invasive specimen for respiratory virus diagnostics but its biochemical complexity challenges direct interfacing with affinity-based biosensors. We report a dual-aptamer magnetic-capture electrochemical assay for detection of influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. For each target virus, two sequence-distinct DNA aptamers are used: an amino-modified capture aptamer (IBV1 or RSV1) covalently coupled to ∼5 μm polydopamine-coated magnetic microparticles by direct Schiff-base reaction with the polydopamine quinone/catechol surface, and a thiol-modified detection aptamer (IBV2 or RSV2) self-assembled on screen-printed gold electrodes via thiol-gold chemistry. After a single multiplexed batch capture step with both aptamer-magnetic-particle types, the pellet is split and analysed in parallel on the two aptamer-modified electrodes by square-wave voltammetry (SWV). Langmuir analysis of the SWV calibration curves yielded apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV), with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. Log-linear calibration spanned 101-104 PFU mL-1 on both channels (n = 4 concentrations, R2 = 0.995 and 0.990) with sensitivities of 8.58 and 6.61 μA per decade, so that each virus-specific assay covers three orders of magnitude of viral load. The sequence-orthogonal dual-aptamer geometry-capture and detection recognitions targeting non-identical epitopes-is proposed as the structural mitigation. This proof-of-concept establishes a programmable, saliva-compatible architecture reconfigurable for emerging respiratory pathogens by aptamer substitution alone.

title_zh: 双适体磁性捕获和电化学检测人工唾液中的 B 型流感病毒和 呼吸道合胞病毒。
source_body_en: Saliva is a promising non-invasive specimen for respiratory virus diagnostics but its biochemical complexity challenges direct interfacing with affinity-based biosensors. We report a dual-aptamer magnetic-capture electrochemical assay for detection of influenza B virus (IBV) and human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) in artificial saliva. For each target virus, two sequence-distinct DNA aptamers are used: an amino-modified capture aptamer (IBV1 or RSV1) covalently coupled to ∼5 μm polydopamine-coated magnetic microparticles by direct Schiff-base reaction with the polydopamine quinone/catechol surface, and a thiol-modified detection aptamer (IBV2 or RSV2) self-assembled on screen-printed gold electrodes via thiol-gold chemistry. After a single multiplexed batch capture step with both aptamer-magnetic-particle types, the pellet is split and analysed in parallel on the two aptamer-modified electrodes by square-wave voltammetry (SWV). Langmuir analysis of the SWV calibration curves yielded apparent dissociation constants of Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) and 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV), with detection limits of 15 and 11 PFU mL-1, respectively. Log-linear calibration spanned 101-104 PFU mL-1 on both channels (n = 4 concentrations, R2 = 0.995 and 0.990) with sensitivities of 8.58 and 6.61 μA per decade, so that each virus-specific assay covers three orders of magnitude of viral load. The sequence-orthogonal dual-aptamer geometry-capture and detection recognitions targeting non-identical epitopes-is proposed as the structural mitigation. This proof-of-concept establishes a programmable, saliva-compatible architecture reconfigurable for emerging respiratory pathogens by aptamer substitution alone.
abstract_zh: 唾液是一种很有前途的呼吸道病毒诊断非侵入性样本,但其生化复杂性挑战了与基于亲和力的生物传感器的直接连接。我们报告了一种双适体磁捕获电化学测定法,用于检测人工唾液中的乙型流感病毒(IBV)和人 呼吸道合胞病毒(hRSV)。对于每种目标病毒,使用两个序列不同的DNA适体:氨基修饰的捕获适体(IBV1或RSV1)通过与聚多巴胺醌/儿茶酚表面的直接席夫碱反应共价偶联至~5μm聚多巴胺包被的磁性微粒,以及硫醇修饰的检测适体(IBV2或RSV2)通过丝网印刷金电极自组装硫醇-金化学。在使用两种适体磁性颗粒类型进行单一多重批量捕获步骤后,将颗粒分开并通过方波伏安法 (SWV) 在两个适体修饰的电极上并行分析。SWV 校准曲线的 Langmuir 分析得出表观解离常数 Kd = 177 ± 62 PFU mL-1 (IBV) 和 226 ± 85 PFU mL-1 (hRSV),检测限分别为 15 和 11 PFU mL-1。对数线性校准在两个通道上的范围为 101-104 PFU mL-1(n = 4 个浓度,R2 = 0.995 和 0.990),灵敏度为每十年 8.58 和 6.61 μA,因此每个病毒特异性检测涵盖三个数量级的病毒载量。序列-正交双适体几何结构-针对不同表位的捕获和检测识别-被提议作为结构缓解。这一概念验证建立了一种可编程的、唾液兼容的架构,可仅通过适体替换来针对新出现的呼吸道病原体进行重新配置。

title: Actin remodeling by human RNA virus: mechanisms and targeted intervention
abstract: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

analysis.scope_and_question: The article examines the molecular mechanisms by which human RNA viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), hijack the host actin network to influence viral replication and transmission efficiency. It focuses on the role of actin remodeling as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, with an emphasis on RSV and its impact on disease progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a comprehensive analysis of the actin cytoskeleton's role in RNA viral infection, including the mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses, including RSV, manipulate host actin dynamics. The review highlights the importance of actin in viral infection and summarizes recent advances in understanding these interactions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Actin remodeling is a critical host mechanism that RNA viruses, including RSV, exploit to enhance their replication and transmission efficiency. The review identifies key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics and outlines the pathways by which RSV and other viruses manipulate the host actin network.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that while actin remodeling is well-established as a host mechanism for RNA viruses, the clinical application of targeting actin signaling pathways remains challenging due to difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. There is also a need for further research on antiviral compounds that specifically target actin-related pathways in RSV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the potential of targeting host factors like actin signaling pathways for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. It suggests that future research should focus on developing antiviral compounds that effectively modulate actin dynamics without causing significant cytotoxicity, particularly for RSV.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the molecular mechanisms by which respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other human RNA viruses manipulate the host actin network to enhance replication and transmission. It highlights the central role of actin remodeling in viral infection and identifies key regulatory molecules involved in this process. The article also discusses the potential of targeting actin signaling pathways for antiviral interventions, while noting the challenges in balancing efficacy and cytotoxicity. Future research is recommended to develop specific antiviral compounds that modulate actin dynamics without harmful side effects, offering a promising strategy for combating RSV and other RNA viruses.

title_zh: 人类RNA病毒对肌动蛋白的重塑:机制和靶向干预
source_body_en: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.
abstract_zh: 肌动蛋白细胞骨架是真核细胞中一个核心的动态网络,维持细胞形态、运动和细胞内运输。大量研究已证实肌动蛋白在RNA病毒感染中的重要性。肌动蛋白重塑作为RNA病毒利用的核心宿主机制,强烈影响病毒复制和传播效率。本文综述了参与肌动蛋白动态调控的关键调节分子。在此基础上,我们重点探讨了六种代表性人类RNA病毒(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒-2、流感A病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、登革热病毒、埃博拉病毒和人类免疫缺陷病毒)劫持宿主肌动蛋白网络的分子机制,揭示了RNA病毒倾向于选择的肌动蛋白劫持途径。最后,我们进一步总结了当前针对抗病毒药物化合物作用于肌动蛋白信号通路的研究现状。鉴于针对宿主因子具有独特的广谱抗病毒药物活性优势,该策略为克服高病毒突变率导致的药物耐受性提供了希望。然而,其临床应用仍面临平衡细胞毒性与疗效的困难。本文旨在为针对肌动蛋白的新型抗病毒药物干预方法提供概念框架。

title: IL-33 signaling uncouples pulmonary regulatory T-cell specialization from suppressive function during type 2 inflammation
abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (TREG) cells are critical mediators of mucosal homeostasis, yet how they fail to restrain exaggerated type 2 immune responses remains poorly understood. This question is exemplified by neonatal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, which is strongly associated with asthma susceptibility later in life despite the persistent presence of pulmonary TREG cells. Here, using complementary murine neonatal RSV infection and allergic airway inflammation models, we identify an IL-33–IL-4Rα signaling axis that reprograms pulmonary TREG-cell function. Mechanistically, IL-33 increased IL-4Rα expression, enhancing glycolysis-dependent STAT6 signaling and promoting GATA3-dependent functional specialization of pulmonary TREG cells. Functionally, IL-33 promoted the expansion and persistence of long-lived pulmonary TH2 cells while simultaneously licensing IL-4-dependent loss of TREG-cell suppressive function. These findings identify IL-33 as a developmental checkpoint that coordinately programs pathogenic TH2 memory and dysfunctional pulmonary TREG cell responses following exaggerated pathogenic type 2 responses.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used complementary murine neonatal RSV infection and allergic airway inflammation models to investigate the role of IL-33–IL-4Rα signaling in reprogramming pulmonary TREG-cell function.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed murine models of neonatal RSV infection and allergic airway inflammation to identify the IL-33–IL-4Rα signaling axis and its effects on pulmonary TREG-cell function.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the mechanisms underlying the failure of TREG cells to suppress type 2 inflammation, which could inform future strategies for asthma prevention and treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on murine models, which may not fully translate to human conditions, and the evidence is derived from abstract-only data, limiting the confidence in the findings.

The research uses murine models to identify an IL-33–IL-4Rα signaling axis that reprograms pulmonary TREG-cell function. The results show that IL-33 enhances glycolysis-dependent STAT6 signaling and promotes GATA3-dependent functional specialization of TREG cells. The authors interpret these findings as identifying IL-33 as a developmental checkpoint that programs pathogenic TH2 memory and dysfunctional TREG responses. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform asthma prevention and treatment strategies. However, the findings are based on murine models and abstract-only data, which limits their applicability to human conditions and reduces confidence in the conclusions.

title_zh: IL-33 信号传导使肺调节性 T 细胞的特化与 2 型炎症期间的抑制功能脱钩
source_body_en: Abstract Regulatory T (TREG) cells are critical mediators of mucosal homeostasis, yet how they fail to restrain exaggerated type 2 immune responses remains poorly understood. This question is exemplified by neonatal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, which is strongly associated with asthma susceptibility later in life despite the persistent presence of pulmonary TREG cells. Here, using complementary murine neonatal RSV infection and allergic airway inflammation models, we identify an IL-33–IL-4Rα signaling axis that reprograms pulmonary TREG-cell function. Mechanistically, IL-33 increased IL-4Rα expression, enhancing glycolysis-dependent STAT6 signaling and promoting GATA3-dependent functional specialization of pulmonary TREG cells. Functionally, IL-33 promoted the expansion and persistence of long-lived pulmonary TH2 cells while simultaneously licensing IL-4-dependent loss of TREG-cell suppressive function. These findings identify IL-33 as a developmental checkpoint that coordinately programs pathogenic TH2 memory and dysfunctional pulmonary TREG cell responses following exaggerated pathogenic type 2 responses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 调节性 T (TREG) 细胞是粘膜稳态的关键介质,但它们如何无法抑制过度的 2 型 免疫应答 仍知之甚少。新生儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染就说明了这个问题,尽管肺部 TREG 细胞持续存在,但这种感染与以后的哮喘易感性密切相关。在这里,利用互补的小鼠新生儿 RSV 感染和过敏性气道炎症模型,我们确定了重新编程肺 TREG 细胞功能的 IL-33–IL-4Rα 信号轴。从机制上讲,IL-33 增加 IL-4Rα 表达,增强糖酵解依赖性 STAT6 信号传导并促进肺 TREG 细胞的 GATA3 依赖性功能特化。从功能上讲,IL-33 促进长寿命肺 TH2 细胞的扩增和持续存在,同时允许 IL-4 依赖性的 TREG 细胞抑制功能丧失。这些发现将 IL-33 确定为一个发育检查点,可协调编程致病性 TH2 记忆和过度致病性 2 型反应后功能失调的肺 TREG 细胞反应。

title: A Narrative Review of the Role of Adjuvants in Adult RSV Vaccines
abstract: The development of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines has advanced substantially in recent years, with three prefusion F (preF) protein-based and mRNA platforms achieving regulatory approval for use in older adults. Among licensed protein subunit vaccines, key design differences include the use of adjuvants and antigen valency, raising important questions regarding the necessity and impact of adjuvantation for RSV prevention. This narrative review examines the role of adjuvants in RSV vaccine development, with a focus on immunogenicity, vaccine effectiveness, safety, and implications for older adults and immunocompromised (IC) populations. Adjuvants can sometimes enhance immune responses but may increase reactogenicity. Clinical trials and observational studies demonstrate that both adjuvanted (RSVPreF3/AS01E) and non-adjuvanted (bivalent RSVpreF) vaccines provide substantial and comparable protection against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization with comparable safety. The totality of evidence to date does not suggest an effectiveness advantage for adjuvanted vaccines among IC populations. Overall, these findings suggest that effective protection against RSV disease in adults can be achieved with or without adjuvantation.

title_zh: 佐剂在成人 RSV 中作用的叙述回顾 疫苗
source_body_en: The development of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines has advanced substantially in recent years, with three prefusion F (preF) protein-based and mRNA platforms achieving regulatory approval for use in older adults. Among licensed protein subunit vaccines, key design differences include the use of adjuvants and antigen valency, raising important questions regarding the necessity and impact of adjuvantation for RSV prevention. This narrative review examines the role of adjuvants in RSV vaccine development, with a focus on immunogenicity, vaccine effectiveness, safety, and implications for older adults and immunocompromised (IC) populations. Adjuvants can sometimes enhance immune responses but may increase reactogenicity. Clinical trials and observational studies demonstrate that both adjuvanted (RSVPreF3/AS01E) and non-adjuvanted (bivalent RSVpreF) vaccines provide substantial and comparable protection against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and hospitalization with comparable safety. The totality of evidence to date does not suggest an effectiveness advantage for adjuvanted vaccines among IC populations. Overall, these findings suggest that effective protection against RSV disease in adults can be achieved with or without adjuvantation.
abstract_zh: 近年来,呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗 的开发取得了实质性进展,三个基于预融合 F (preF) 蛋白和 mRNA 的平台获得了监管部门批准用于老年人。在获得许可的蛋白质亚基 疫苗 中,关键的设计差异包括佐剂的使用和抗原效价,这引发了有关佐剂预防 RSV 的必要性和影响的重要问题。这篇叙述性综述探讨了佐剂在 RSV 疫苗 发育中的作用,重点是免疫原性、疫苗 的有效性、安全性以及对老年人和免疫功能低下 (IC) 人群的影响。佐剂有时可以增强 免疫应答,但可能会增加反应原性。临床试验和观察性研究表明,佐剂(RSVPreF3/AS01E)和非佐剂(二价RSVpreF)疫苗 均可针对 RSV 相关下呼吸道疾病和住院提供实质性且可比的保护,且安全性相当。迄今为止的全部证据并未表明佐剂 疫苗 在 IC 人群中具有有效性优势。总体而言,这些研究结果表明,无论有或没有辅助治疗,都可以有效预防成人 RSV 疾病。

title: 6-Substituted 7-Deazapurine Ribonucleosides Capable of Non-canonical Base Recognition as Inhibitors of Respiratory RNA Viruses.
abstract: Most nucleoside antiviral analogues mimic canonical Watson-Crick base pairing to increase their likelihood of recognition and incorporation by replicative enzymes into a growing viral nucleic acid strand. Herein, we investigated whether non-canonical base recognition principles based on either shape complementarity or non-hydrogen bond interactions could also be exploited to generate novel small-molecule antivirals. Thus, the exogenous amino group of 7-deazaadenosine was systematically replaced with various 6-alkyl and 6-alkynyl substituents to assess their impact on antiviral activity against RNA respiratory viruses, including influenza A and B, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Sub-micromolar potency was observed for multiple compounds, with minimal cytotoxicity and inhibition of host DNA polymerases. Notably, the different modifications profoundly affected the antiviral spectrum, suggesting that despite lacking a hydrogen-bond donor, analogues with either 6-alkyl or 6-alkynyl substituents likely engage polymerases through distinct recognition mechanisms.

title_zh: 6-取代的 7-脱氮嘌呤核糖核苷能够进行非规范碱基识别,作为呼吸道 RNA 病毒的抑制剂。
source_body_en: Most nucleoside antiviral analogues mimic canonical Watson-Crick base pairing to increase their likelihood of recognition and incorporation by replicative enzymes into a growing viral nucleic acid strand. Herein, we investigated whether non-canonical base recognition principles based on either shape complementarity or non-hydrogen bond interactions could also be exploited to generate novel small-molecule antivirals. Thus, the exogenous amino group of 7-deazaadenosine was systematically replaced with various 6-alkyl and 6-alkynyl substituents to assess their impact on antiviral activity against RNA respiratory viruses, including influenza A and B, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). abstract_zh: 大多数核苷 抗病毒药物 类似物模仿典型的 Watson-Crick 碱基配对,以增加其被复制酶识别和掺入不断生长的病毒核酸链的可能性。在此,我们研究了是否也可以利用基于形状互补或非氢键相互作用的非规范碱基识别原理来生成新型小分子 抗病毒药物。因此,7-脱氮腺苷的外源氨基被系统地替换为各种6-烷基和6-炔基取代基,以评估它们对抗病毒药物针对RNA呼吸道病毒(包括甲型和乙型流感、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)、中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒(MERS-CoV)和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV))活性的影响。多种化合物均具有亚微摩尔效力,且具有最小的细胞毒性和对 宿主 DNA 聚合酶的抑制作用。值得注意的是,不同的修饰深刻地影响了 抗病毒药物 谱,这表明尽管缺乏氢键供体,但具有 6-烷基或 6-炔基取代基的类似物可能通过不同的识别机制与聚合酶结合。

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4 + T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4 + responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4 + response was strongly T helper 1 (T H 1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T H 2 cytokines. Both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然对健康构成威胁,特别是对于婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下的个体。尽管中和抗体可以帮助限制感染和病毒复制,但 T 细胞对于减轻疾病严重程度至关重要。评估与年龄相关的 T 细胞功能下降对于 疫苗 评估非常重要。我们使用细胞内细胞因子染色、激活诱导标记、Meso Scale Discovery 测定和单细胞多组学分析来评估年轻人和老年人中的 RSV 疫苗 mRNA-1345 反应。mRNA-1345 在两个 队列研究 中诱导了相当的 CD4 + 和 CD8 + T 细胞反应,CD4 + 反应持续 24 个月。CD4 + 反应是强烈的 T 辅助细胞 1 (TH 1) 极化,干扰素 γ、白细胞介素 2 和肿瘤坏死因子 α 增加,而 T H 2 细胞因子最少。CD4 + 和 CD8 + T 细胞均显示出多功能性的增加,并且在 2 年后仍保持较高水平。单细胞和 T 细胞受体库分析显示,不同年龄组的 Pre-F 特异性表型、转录谱和克隆重叠相似,支持 mRNA-1345 疫苗接种 后强大、持久的细胞免疫。这些发现表明,成人中共有 疫苗 引发的 T 细胞免疫。

abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally prevalent respiratory pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections across all age groups, with the greatest disease burden in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Clinical manifestations range from mild upper respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and sore throat, to severe lower respiratory tract disease such as bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and secondary bacterial infections that may require intensive care and mechanical ventilation. Despite its widespread circulation and substantial healthcare impact, important aspects of hMPV transmission, pathogenesis, and host immune responses remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective therapeutics and vaccines. This review summarizes the current knowledge of hMPV epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, pathogenesis, and prevention strategies, with emphasis on recent outbreaks that highlight its seasonal and geographic variability. We discuss the viral life cycle and the contributions of the major surface glycoproteins—fusion (F), attachment (G), and small hydrophobic (SH) proteins—to viral infectivity, immune evasion, and disease progression. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), next-generation sequencing, metagenomic approaches, and nanopore sequencing, are also examined. While supportive care remains the cornerstone of clinical management, existing antiviral therapies demonstrate limited and inconsistent efficacy. Emerging preventive and therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-based vaccines and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, offer promising avenues for disease control. Improved understanding of hMPV biology and host-pathogen interactions will be critical for developing effective interventions to reduce the global burden of this increasingly recognized respiratory pathogen.

title: Rapid and sensitive on-chip microcapillary electrophoresis for discrete SARS-CoV-2 immunocomplex diagnostics
abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and quantitative molecular diagnostics remain in sustained demand, driving the development of miniaturized analytical platforms. Conventional rapid antigen tests rely on lateral-flow techniques, requiring capture and detection antibodies, gold nanoparticle labels, and precise binding kinetics to generate a visible signal. Microcapillary electrophoresis (μCE) is well established for genomic DNA separation, yet its extension to protein analysis remains limited. Here we report a μCE method for rapid separation and detection of SARS-CoV-2 immunocomplexes, using a polymethyl methacrylate microfluidic chip filled with 5.5% linear polyacrylamide as the sieving matrix to perform an on-chip immunoassay. Unlike lateral-flow formats, our platform requires only a single fluorescently labeled antibody, with a positive or negative result read directly from the presence or absence of an immunocomplex peak. Fluorescently labeled antibodies were incubated with SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (Np) to form immunocomplexes, the bound complex was resolved from free antibody within 30 s, based on the difference in electrophoretic mobility caused by altered charge-to-size ratio. Fluorescence signals were acquired by fluorescence microscopy and processed with a custom Python pipeline for electropherogram analysis and peak profiling. The assay resolved Np antigen across the alpha, beta, and delta variants and produced consistent, reproducible signals from clinical oropharyngeal swab specimens, achieving a detection limit of 5 μg/mL with minimal reagent consumption. Specificity was confirmed against a panel of common respiratory pathogens, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, or influenza virus, with no visible immunocomplex peak indicating negligible cross-reactivity. Its sub-minute separation time and compatibility with automation position this μCE platform as a scalable route to decentralized point-of-care testing and screening for infectious diseases.

abstract_zh: 快速、灵敏和定量的分子诊断仍然具有持续的需求,推动了小型化分析平台的发展。传统的快速抗原测试依赖于侧流技术,需要捕获和检测抗体、金纳米颗粒标记以及精确的结合动力学来产生可见信号。微毛细管电泳 (μCE) 已广泛用于基因组 DNA 分离,但其在蛋白质分析方面的扩展仍然有限。在此,我们报道了一种快速分离和检测 SARS-CoV-2 免疫复合物的 μCE 方法,使用填充有 5.5% 线性聚丙烯酰胺的聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯微流控芯片作为筛分基质进行片上免疫分析。与侧流格式不同,我们的平台仅需要单个荧光标记抗体,可直接根据免疫复合物峰的存在或不存在读取阳性或阴性结果。将荧光标记的抗体与 SARS-CoV-2 核衣壳蛋白 (Np) 一起孵育,形成免疫复合物,根据电荷尺寸比改变引起的电泳迁移率差异,在 30 秒内将结合的复合物与游离抗体分离。通过荧光显微镜采集荧光信号,并使用自定义 Python 管道进行处理以进行电泳图分析和峰分析。该检测可解析 α、β 和 δ 变体中的 Np 抗原,并从临床口咽拭子样本中产生一致、可重复的信号,以最少的试剂消耗实现 5 μg/mL 的检测限。证实了针对一组常见呼吸道病原体、呼吸道合胞病毒、腺病毒或流感病毒的特异性,没有可见的免疫复合物峰,表明交叉反应性可以忽略不计。其亚分钟的分离时间以及与自动化的兼容性使该 μCE 平台成为分散式即时检测和传染病筛查的可扩展途径。

title: TRIM69 Suppresses the Cellular AMPK Pathway to Inhibit Viral Replication
abstract: Interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) mount an antiviral defense by targeting both viral components and cellular pathways required for infection. Here, we show that the interferon- and virus-inducible antiviral factor TRIM69 suppresses cellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling and restricts replication of both RNA and DNA viruses. Ectopic expression of TRIM69 inhibited Sendai virus (SeV)-induced autophagy and suppressed phosphorylation of AMPK and its downstream target, ULK1, in response to viral infection and nutrient deprivation. Consistent with inhibition of this proviral AMPK signaling pathway, TRIM69 expression strongly restricted replication of paramyxoviruses and pneumoviruses, including SeV, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV3), and herpesviruses, e.g., herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). Consistent with these findings, knockdown of endogenous TRIM69 enhanced viral replication, demonstrating a physiological antiviral role for TRIM69. In addition to suppressing viral replication, TRIM69 supported the expression of antiviral genes, including IFNB1, IFIT2, and IFIT3, suggesting amplification of the innate antiviral signaling. Together, these findings identify TRIM69 as a broad antiviral ISG that targets the cellular AMPK pathway and contributes to host innate immune responses against viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of TRIM69 in antiviral defense by targeting cellular pathways required for viral infection, addressing the need to understand how ISGs contribute to host innate immune responses against viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the use of ectopic expression of TRIM69 and knockdown of endogenous TRIM69 in cell lines to examine the effects on viral replication and cellular signaling pathways.
analysis.methods: TRIM69 was ectopically expressed and endogenous TRIM69 was knocked down to assess its impact on viral replication and cellular AMPK signaling. Assays included monitoring of autophagy, AMPK phosphorylation, and viral replication in response to viral infection and nutrient deprivation.
analysis.main_results: TRIM69 inhibited Sendai virus-induced autophagy and suppressed AMPK phosphorylation and its downstream target ULK1. TRIM69 strongly restricted replication of paramyxoviruses, pneumoviruses, and herpesviruses, including Sendai virus, respiratory syncytial virus, human parainfluenza virus type 3, and herpes simplex virus type 1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that TRIM69 targets the cellular AMPK pathway to restrict viral replication, providing a novel mechanism for ISG-mediated antiviral defense.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: TRIM69 supports the expression of antiviral genes and amplifies innate antiviral signaling, which could inform the development of therapeutic strategies to enhance host innate immune responses against viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of cell lines and the absence of in vivo models, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of randomized controlled trials and animal models.

analysis.summary_en: This study demonstrated that TRIM69, an interferon- and virus-inducible antiviral factor, targets the cellular AMPK pathway to restrict viral replication. TRIM69 also supports the expression of antiviral genes, suggesting a novel mechanism for ISG-mediated antiviral defense.

title: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
abstract: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

title: Is Wastewater Surveillance Predictive during the Endemic Phase of Respiratory Disease? An Analysis Based on Clinical, Wastewater, and Digital Search Data in Detroit, Michigan
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.
abstract_zh: 基于废水的 流行病学 (WBE) 已成为 COVID-19 大流行催化的一项重大公共卫生创新。然而,在 COVID-19 流行期间和之后,其潜力仍未得到充分开发。本研究评估了 WBE 识别 COVID-19 大流行向地方流行转变的潜力,并在大流行后时代跨多个 监测 系统针对甲型流感 (IAV) 和乙型流感 (IBV)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 提供早期预警。我们从 2020 年 4 月 8 日到 2025 年 7 月 31 日监测了废水中的 SARS-CoV-2 N1 浓度,生成了密歇根州底特律最早且运行时间最长的废水数据集。采用峰值识别方法,通过比较各阶段之间 N1 浓度峰值的频率来识别大流行到地方病的转变。在流行阶段,从2022年10月1日到2025年3月31日,我们监测了底特律废水中的RSV、IAV、IBV和SARS-CoV-2。采用皮尔逊相关系数来量化废水浓度与临床、症状和数字流行病学数据之间的关联。时滞互相关 (TLCC) 用于检查这些数据集之间的时间动态,并确定每种疾病和时滞的最早出现的数据。我们进行了广泛的文献研究,以阐明每种疾病的时滞机制,包括 TLCC 结果。基于 WBE 数据集建立随机森林模型来预测临床病例。这是首批使用基于 WBE 的方法来识别 SARS-CoV-2 从大流行向地方流行转变的研究之一。在这些呼吸道疾病的流行阶段,系统地分析了废水数据与传统临床、症状和数字流行病学 监测 数据的关系。这项研究证明了 WBE 在流行阶段的预测价值,为季节性呼吸道疾病(包括 COVID-19、流感和流感样疾病)提供早期预警和预测。

title: Respiratory pathogen profiles in children aged 0–18 years: a single-center experience (October 2024 – June 2025)
abstract: Distinguishing active pediatric respiratory infection from upper respiratory tract colonization and interpreting etiology from routine host laboratory markers remains a significant clinical challenge. This study evaluated the detection spectrum of pediatric respiratory pathogens and examined exploratory associations with routine inflammatory and hematological biomarkers. A retrospective surveillance of 784 PCR-positive pediatric cases (aged 0–18 years) was conducted between October 2024 and June 2025. Pathogen profiles, temporal dynamics, codetection patterns, and associations with C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) were evaluated. Multiplex PCR revealed a polymorphic landscape with a 51.7% codetection rate. Viruses predominated (60.5%), led by rhinovirus/enterovirus (32.1%), influenza viruses (26.1%), RSV (16.6%), and adenovirus (14.8%). pneumoniae (38.9%) and H. influenzae (31.6%) were the most prevalent bacterial targets among expanded panel tests. Influenza detections were associated with significantly lower median ANC ( p < 0.001), whereas adenovirus showed elevated CRP and ANC ( p < 0.001). Mycoplasma pneumoniae exhibited elevated CRP and relative lymphopenia ( p < 0.001). pneumoniae detection showed no significant correlation with CRP elevation ( p = 0.181), whereas H. influenzae was associated with higher median CRP levels ( p < 0.001). Routine host biomarkers demonstrate distinct observational associations across viral and bacterial PCR detection groups. However, molecular detection of commensal bacteria on nasopharyngeal specimens must be interpreted cautiously alongside systemic inflammatory markers to avoid overattributing active disease to simple colonization.
