analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the clinical challenge of distinguishing active pediatric respiratory infections from upper respiratory tract colonization and interpreting etiology from routine host laboratory markers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective surveillance of 784 PCR-positive pediatric cases (aged 0–18 years) was conducted between October 2024 and June 2025.
analysis.methods: Multiplex PCR was used to evaluate pathogen profiles, temporal dynamics, codetection patterns, and associations with C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and absolute lymphocyte count (ALC).
analysis.main_results: Viruses predominated (60.5%), with rhinovirus/enterovirus (32.1%), influenza viruses (26.1%), RSV (16.6%), and adenovirus (14.8%) being the most common. pneumoniae (38.9%) and H. influenzae (31.6%) were also detected. Influenza detections were associated with significantly lower median ANC ( p < 0.001), while adenovirus showed elevated CRP and ANC ( p < 0.001). pneumoniae exhibited elevated CRP and relative lymphopenia ( p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found distinct observational associations of routine host biomarkers across viral and bacterial PCR detection groups, highlighting the need for cautious interpretation of commensal bacteria alongside systemic inflammatory markers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for pediatric respiratory infections, particularly in distinguishing active infections from colonization.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for bias in PCR detection. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

The findings can inform surveillance and diagnosis of pediatric respiratory infections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决区分活动性小儿呼吸道感染和上呼吸道定植以及从常规 宿主 实验室标志物解释病因的临床挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 监测 于 2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 6 月期间对 784 例 PCR 阳性儿科病例(0-18 岁)进行了回顾性研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多重 PCR 评估病原体谱、时间动态、联合检测模式以及与 C 反应蛋白 (CRP)、白蛋白、绝对中性粒细胞计数 (ANC) 和绝对淋巴细胞计数 (ALC) 的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 病毒占主导地位(60.5%),其中鼻病毒/肠道病毒(32.1%)、流感病毒(26.1%)、RSV(16.6%)和腺病毒(14.8%)最常见。还检测到肺炎衣原体(38.9%)和流感嗜血杆菌(31.6%)。流感检测与中位 ANC 显着降低相关 (p < 0.001),而腺病毒则显示 CRP 和 ANC 升高 (p < 0.001)。肺炎链球菌表现出 CRP 升高和相对淋巴细胞减少 (p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,病毒和细菌 PCR 检测组中常规 宿主 生物标志物存在明显的观察关联,这凸显了对共生细菌与全身炎症标志物进行谨慎解释的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测、诊断 和 治疗 治疗儿科呼吸道感染的策略提供参考,特别是在区分活动性感染和定植方面。

title_zh: 0-18岁儿童呼吸道病原体概况:单中心经验(2024年10月-2025年6月)
source_body_en: Distinguishing active pediatric respiratory infection from upper respiratory tract colonization and interpreting etiology from routine host laboratory markers remains a significant clinical challenge. This study evaluated the detection spectrum of pediatric respiratory pathogens and examined exploratory associations with routine inflammatory and hematological biomarkers. A retrospective surveillance of 784 PCR-positive pediatric cases (aged 0–18 years) was conducted between October 2024 and June 2025. Pathogen profiles, temporal dynamics, codetection patterns, and associations with C-reactive protein (CRP), albumin, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) were evaluated. Multiplex PCR revealed a polymorphic landscape with a 51.7% codetection rate. Viruses predominated (60.5%), led by rhinovirus/enterovirus (32.1%), influenza viruses (26.1%), RSV (16.6%), and adenovirus (14.8%). pneumoniae (38.9%) and H. influenzae (31.6%) were the most prevalent bacterial targets among expanded panel tests. Influenza detections were associated with significantly lower median ANC ( p < 0.001), whereas adenovirus showed elevated CRP and ANC ( p < 0.001). Mycoplasma pneumoniae exhibited elevated CRP and relative lymphopenia ( p < 0.001). pneumoniae detection showed no significant correlation with CRP elevation ( p = 0.181), whereas H. influenzae was associated with higher median CRP levels ( p < 0.001). Routine host biomarkers demonstrate distinct observational associations across viral and bacterial PCR detection groups. However, molecular detection of commensal bacteria on nasopharyngeal specimens must be interpreted cautiously alongside systemic inflammatory markers to avoid overattributing active disease to simple colonization.
abstract_zh: 区分活动性小儿呼吸道感染与上呼吸道定植并根据常规 宿主 实验室标志物解释病因仍然是一项重大的临床挑战。这项研究评估了儿科呼吸道病原体的检测谱,并检查了与常规炎症和血液生物标志物的探索性关联。2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 6 月期间,对 784 例 PCR 阳性儿科病例(0-18 岁)进行了 监测 回顾性研究。评估了病原体谱、时间动态、联合检测模式以及与 C 反应蛋白 (CRP)、白蛋白、绝对中性粒细胞计数 (ANC) 和绝对淋巴细胞计数 (ALC) 的关联。多重 PCR 显示多态性,共检测率为 51.7%。病毒占主导地位(60.5%),其中鼻病毒/肠道病毒(32.1%)、流感病毒(26.1%)、RSV(16.6%)和腺病毒(14.8%)为首。肺炎链球菌 (38.9%) 和流感嗜血杆菌 (31.6%) 是扩展小组测试中最常见的细菌目标。流感检测与中位 ANC 显着降低相关 (p < 0.001),而腺病毒则显示 CRP 和 ANC 升高 (p < 0.001)。肺炎支原体表现出 CRP 升高和相对淋巴细胞减少 (p < 0.001)。肺炎链球菌检测与 CRP 升高无显着相关性 (p = 0.181),而流感嗜血杆菌检测与较高的中位 CRP 水平相关 (p < 0.001)。常规 宿主 生物标志物表现出病毒和细菌 PCR 检测组之间不同的观察关联。然而,鼻咽标本上共生细菌的分子检测必须与全身炎症标志物一起谨慎解释,以避免将活动性疾病过度归因于简单的定植。

title: From Concept to Clinical Trial: Starting Clinical Trials with a New Vaccine
abstract: Abstract Vaccine development is complex, and there are many things that need to be taken into consideration at every step. The vaccine needs to address an unmet medical need that can be measured in a pivotal phase 3 study. A Target Product Profile (TPP) and a Clinical Development Plan (CDP) are critical for planning. A Quality Management System (QMS) is required, with standard operating procedures (SOP) based on International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) guidance and compliant with national laws and regulations. The Investigator Brochure (IB) informs investigators and site staff about clinical aspects of the study vaccine. Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) must be manufactured and released, and toxicology data must be generated, all within quality systems. There are many options for the design of a first-in-human (FIH) phase 1 vaccine clinical trial to be covered in the Clinical Trial Protocol (CTP). We compare recent FIH studies of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines delivering prefusion F antigen to illustrate some options. Once the protocol is final, Informed Consent Documents (ICD), site management plans and other study-related documents must be prepared. Regulatory and ethics committee applications must be submitted and approved, and clinical trial sites prepared. The FIH study provides medical and financial justification for progressing into larger clinical trials, so it is usually performed under pressure to deliver rapid results but also must meet rigorous ethical, safety and quality standards.

title_zh: 从概念到临床试验:用新的疫苗开始临床试验
source_body_en: Abstract Vaccine development is complex, and there are many things that need to be taken into consideration at every step. The vaccine needs to address an unmet medical need that can be measured in a pivotal phase 3 study. A Target Product Profile (TPP) and a Clinical Development Plan (CDP) are critical for planning. A Quality Management System (QMS) is required, with standard operating procedures (SOP) based on International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) guidance and compliant with national laws and regulations. The Investigator Brochure (IB) informs investigators and site staff about clinical aspects of the study vaccine. Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) must be manufactured and released, and toxicology data must be generated, all within quality systems. There are many options for the design of a first-in-human (FIH) phase 1 vaccine clinical trial to be covered in the Clinical Trial Protocol (CTP). We compare recent FIH studies of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines delivering prefusion F antigen to illustrate some options. Once the protocol is final, Informed Consent Documents (ICD), site management plans and other study-related documents must be prepared. Regulatory and ethics committee applications must be submitted and approved, and clinical trial sites prepared. The FIH study provides medical and financial justification for progressing into larger clinical trials, so it is usually performed under pressure to deliver rapid results but also must meet rigorous ethical, safety and quality standards.
abstract_zh: 摘要 疫苗的开发很复杂,每一步都需要考虑很多事情。疫苗 需要解决未满足的医疗需求,该需求可以在关键的 3 期研究中进行衡量。目标产品概况 (TPP) 和临床开发计划 (CDP) 对于规划至关重要。需要质量管理体系 (QMS),以及基于国际人用药品技术要求协调委员会 (ICH) 指导的标准操作程序 (SOP),并符合国家法律和法规。研究者手册 (IB) 向研究者和现场工作人员通报研究 疫苗 的临床方面。研究药品 (IMP) 必须在质量体系内生产和发布,并且必须生成毒理学数据。临床试验方案 (CTP) 中涵盖了首次人体 (FIH) 1 期 疫苗 临床试验的设计有多种选择。我们比较了最近关于 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗 提供融合前 F 抗原的 FIH 研究,以说明一些选择。一旦协议最终确定,就必须准备知情同意文件 (ICD)、现场管理计划和其他与研究相关的文件。必须提交监管和伦理委员会的申请并获得批准,并准备好临床试验地点。FIH 研究为进入更大规模的临床试验提供了医学和财务理由,因此通常是在快速得出结果的压力下进行的,但也必须满足严格的道德、安全和质量标准。

title: Comparative clinical, immunological, and pulmonary responses to virulent bovine respiratory syncytial virus infection in colostrum-fed, intranasally vaccinated calves
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare clinical, pulmonary, and immunologic responses to bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV) challenge in colostrum-fed, BRSV-seropositive calves following administration of 2 commercially available intranasal vaccines. Methods 34 male Holstein calves (9 to 20 days old) were randomly assigned to receive vaccine A (Nasalgen; n = 17) or vaccine B (Inforce 3; 17). Nine weeks after vaccination, calves were challenged with virulent BRSV. Clinical observations were recorded daily. Arterial partial pressure of oxygen was measured on day 6 after challenge, and percentage pneumonic lung involvement was assessed at necropsy on day 8. Antibody responses and viral shedding were assessed. Results Clinical signs were infrequent and mild in both groups, and nasal shedding of BRSV was low. Median lung lesion scores were lower in calves receiving vaccine B than in calves receiving vaccine A (2.3% vs 4.6%). Arterial oxygen concentrations were numerically higher in vaccine B calves (median, 91.0 mm Hg) than in vaccine A calves (median, 82.8 mm Hg), although this difference was not significant. A greater proportion of vaccine B calves had Pao 2 values within the normal range (> 87.1 mm Hg) compared to vaccine A calves (12 of 17 [71%] vs 7 of 17 [41%]). Both vaccines induced anamnestic mucosal and systemic antibody responses. Conclusions Both vaccines were associated with minimal clinical disease following BRSV challenge. Clinical Relevance Results suggest a modest advantage of vaccine B with respect to pulmonary involvement and maintenance of arterial oxygenation under these experimental conditions.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association

title: Respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in Malaysian public hospitals: prevalence and epidemiologic patterns from January 2023 until July 2024.
abstract: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice. We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024. Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed. We assessed overall positivity, pathogen frequencies, age-group and regional distributions, and monthly and quarterly trends. A total of 8,361 samples were included, of which 5,252 (62.8%) had at least one pathogen detected. Single detections were identified in 4,279 samples (51.2%), while co-detections were observed in 973 samples (11.6%). Viral pathogens predominated. Rhinovirus/enterovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (23.8%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus A/B (13.7%) and influenza A H1N1/2009 (4.8%). Positivity was highest among children aged 1 to 4 years and infants aged 1 to 11 months, and age-related variation was more pronounced than regional variation. The leading pathogens also demonstrated distinct temporal profiles, with different peak months across the study period. In conclusion, respiratory pathogen detection in this hospital-based population was characterised by a high positivity rate, predominance of viral pathogens, marked age-related differences, and distinct temporal patterns. These findings support the value of multiplex PCR for respiratory pathogen surveillance in Malaysian public hospitals.

title_zh: 马来西亚公立医院通过多重 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病原体:患病率 和 2023 年 1 月至 2024 年 7 月的流行病学模式。
source_body_en: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice. We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024. Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed. We assessed overall positivity, pathogen frequencies, age-group and regional distributions, and monthly and quarterly trends. A total of 8,361 samples were included, of which 5,252 (62.8%) had at least one pathogen detected. Single detections were identified in 4,279 samples (51.2%), while co-detections were observed in 973 samples (11.6%). Viral pathogens predominated. Rhinovirus/enterovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (23.8%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus A/B (13.7%) and influenza A H1N1/2009 (4.8%). Positivity was highest among children aged 1 to 4 years and infants aged 1 to 11 months, and age-related variation was more pronounced than regional variation. The leading pathogens also demonstrated distinct temporal profiles, with different peak months across the study period. In conclusion, respiratory pathogen detection in this hospital-based population was characterised by a high positivity rate, predominance of viral pathogens, marked age-related differences, and distinct temporal patterns. These findings support the value of multiplex PCR for respiratory pathogen surveillance in Malaysian public hospitals.
abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染仍然是住院和诊断不确定性的重要原因,多重聚合酶链反应检测可以在常规临床实践中快速检测多种病原体。我们的目的是描述马来西亚公立医院 QIAstat-Dx 呼吸道 SARS-CoV-2 检测组检测到的呼吸道病原体的 患病率、人口统计学关联和时间趋势。这项多中心回顾性横断面研究包括 2023 年 1 月 1 日至 2024 年 7 月 31 日期间检测的疑似急性呼吸道感染病例的鼻咽拭子样本。使用标准化记录表格从参与地点收集数据并进行分析。我们评估了总体阳性率、病原体频率、年龄组和区域分布以及月度和季度趋势。共纳入 8,361 个样本,其中 5,252 个样本(62.8%)至少检测到一种病原体。在 4,279 个样本 (51.2%) 中发现了单一检测,而在 973 个样本 (11.6%) 中发现了联合检测。病毒病原体占主导地位。鼻病毒/肠道病毒是最常检测到的病原体(23.8%),其次是呼吸道合胞病毒 A/B(13.7%)和甲型H1N1/2009流感(4.8%)。1至4岁儿童和1至11个月婴儿的阳性率最高,且与年龄相关的差异比区域差异更明显。主要病原体还表现出不同的时间特征,在整个研究期间具有不同的高峰月份。总之,该医院人群的呼吸道病原体检测具有阳性率高、病毒病原体占主导地位、明显的年龄相关差异和不同的时间模式的特点。这些研究结果支持了马来西亚公立医院呼吸道病原体 监测 多重 PCR 的价值。

full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide. Although no combination therapies exist for RSV, ribavirin (RBA) and TMC353121 (TMC) can efficiently combat RSV through different mechanisms. We investigated the feasibility of formulating RBA and TMC into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessed its antiviral activity. Our results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies indicated that RTSN exhibited remarkable antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. RTSN showed antiviral efficacy, with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Moreover, RTSN was used to treat a mouse model of the respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP) via multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization, while maintaining promising biosafety. Overall, this study presents an innovative treatment strategy for RSV and highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in augmenting potential. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide. Although no combination therapies exist for RSV, ribavirin (RBA) and TMC353121 (TMC) can efficiently combat RSV through different mechanisms. We investigated the feasibility of formulating RBA and TMC into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessed its antiviral activity. Our results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies indicated that RTSN exhibited remarkable antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. RTSN showed antiviral efficacy, with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Moreover, RTSN was used to treat a mouse model of the respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP) via multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization, while maintaining promising biosafety. Overall, this study presents an innovative treatment strategy for RSV and highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in augmenting potential. title_original: Co-Assembly of Ribavirin and TMC353121 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Inhibition of Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Induced Pneumonia as an Alternative Therapy

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore an alternative therapy for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection by investigating the feasibility of formulating ribavirin and TMC353121 into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessing its antiviral activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the formulation of RBA and TMC into RTSN and assessed its antiviral activity through in vitro and in vivo experiments, including a mouse model of RSV-induced pneumonia.
analysis.methods: The methods included the formulation of ribavirin and TMC353121 into self-assembled nanoparticles, testing their antiviral activity through in vitro assays, and evaluating their efficacy in a mouse model of RSV-induced pneumonia.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. RTSN exhibited antiviral efficacy with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the potential of RTSN as an innovative treatment strategy for RSV, leveraging self-assembly technology to enhance antiviral activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that RTSN could offer a new therapeutic approach for RSV, potentially improving antiviral efficacy and biosafety in treating RSV-induced pneumonia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of a mouse model, which may not fully represent human RSV infection. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of clinical trials and long-term safety data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of ribavirin and TMC353121 self-assembled nanoparticles (RTSN) as an alternative therapy for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The research aimed to assess the feasibility of this formulation and its antiviral activity. Results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions, with antiviral efficacy demonstrated by a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. The authors interpreted these findings as an innovative strategy for RSV treatment, leveraging self-assembly technology. The study's significance lies in its potential to enhance therapeutic options for RSV, particularly in treating RSV-induced pneumonia. However, the study is limited by its reliance on a mouse model, which may not fully reflect human conditions, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the absence of clinical trials and long-term safety data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过研究将利巴韦林和TMC353121配制为RBA-TMC自组装纳米颗粒(RTSN)的可行性并评估其抗病毒药物活性,探索呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染的替代疗法。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及将 RBA 和 TMC 配制到 RTSN 中,并通过体外和体内实验(包括 RSV 诱导肺炎的小鼠模型)评估其 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括将利巴韦林和 TMC353121 配制为自组装纳米颗粒,通过体外测定测试其 抗病毒药物 活性,并评估其在 RSV 诱导肺炎小鼠模型中的功效。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,RBA和TMC通过氢键和π-π堆积相互作用形成RTSN。RTSN 表现出 抗病毒药物 功效,选择性指数为 43.8,有效浓度 (EC50) 为 10.9 μM。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了 RTSN 作为 RSV 创新 治疗 策略的潜力,利用自组装技术增强 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RTSN 可以为 RSV 提供一种新的治疗方法,有可能提高 抗病毒药物 治疗 RSV 引起的肺炎的疗效和生物安全性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其使用小鼠模型而受到限制,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 RSV 感染。由于缺乏临床试验和长期安全性数据,证据不充分。

analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括将利巴韦林和 TMC353121 配制为自组装纳米颗粒,通过体外测定测试其 抗病毒药物 活性,并评估其在 RSV 诱导肺炎小鼠模型中的功效。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,RBA和TMC通过氢键和π-π堆积相互作用形成RTSN。RTSN 表现出 抗病毒药物 功效,选择性指数为 43.8,有效浓度 (EC50) 为 10.9 μM。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了 RTSN 作为 RSV 创新 治疗 策略的潜力,利用自组装技术增强 抗病毒药物 活性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RTSN 可以为 RSV 提供一种新的治疗方法,有可能提高 抗病毒药物 治疗 RSV 引起的肺炎的疗效和生物安全性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其使用小鼠模型而受到限制,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 RSV 感染。由于缺乏临床试验和长期安全性数据,证据不充分。

full_text: Abstract Background Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) is among the major pathogens causing acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children and older adults. The second hypervariable region near the C-terminus of the G gene (HVR2-G) is the target for genotyping that has been used in molecular epidemiology surveillance for nearly 28 years, and a large amount of virological data has been accumulated. Whole-genome sequence (WGS) has been suggested for use in classifying lineages because it has provided the highest resolution since 2020. As such, evaluating the applicability of the HVR2-G sequencing window for lineage classification and integrating previous HVR2-G genotypes with the new WGS-defined lineage nomenclature are needed. Methods The HVR2-G region was extracted from WGS sequences from GenBank and the lineage nomenclature data were downloaded from Nextstrain. Phylogenetic and nucleotide pairwise distance (p-distance) analyses of HVR2-G sequences were conducted using IQ-TREE 2.3.6 and MEGA11.0, respectively. Results Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the primary lineages defined by WGS-defined lineage nomenclature could be classified using the HVR2-G region with a bootstrap over 70%; the nested lineages could not be distinguished. Nineteen and 37 previous HVR2-G genotypes of HRSVA and B were reduced to 4 (A.1, A.2, A.3 and A.D) and 5 (B.1, B.2, B.3, B.4 and B.D) lineages with P-distance thresholds greater than 0.102 and 0.0591, respectively. Conclusion This study verified that the HVR2-G sequencing window provides reliable assignment of major HRSV lineages and enables integration with historical surveillance datasets. It has the potential to serve as a complement to the application of WGS for molecular virological surveillance of HRSV in China and globally, especially in resource-limited areas. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the applicability of the HVR2-G sequencing window for lineage classification and integrate previous HVR2-G genotypes with the new WGS-defined lineage nomenclature. Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) is a major pathogen causing acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children and older adults.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using whole-genome sequence (WGS) data from GenBank and lineage nomenclature data from Nextstrain. The HVR2-G region was extracted from these sequences to assess its utility in lineage classification.
analysis.methods: The HVR2-G region was extracted from WGS sequences from GenBank and the lineage nomenclature data were downloaded from Nextstrain. Phylogenetic and nucleotide pairwise distance (p-distance) analyses of HVR2-G sequences were conducted using IQ-TREE 2.3.6 and MEGA11.0, respectively.
analysis.main_results: Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the primary lineages defined by WGS-defined lineage nomenclature could be classified using the HVR2-G region with a bootstrap over 70%; the nested lineages could not be distinguished. Nineteen and 37 previous HVR2-G genotypes of HRSVA and B were reduced to 4 (A.1, A.2, A.3 and A.D) and 5 (B.1, B.2, B.3, B.4 and B.D) lineages with P-distance thresholds greater than 0.102 and 0.0591, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study confirmed that the HVR2-G sequencing window provides reliable assignment of major HRSV lineages and enables integration with historical surveillance datasets. This approach has the potential to serve as a complement to the application of WGS for molecular virological surveillance of HRSV in China and globally, especially in resource-limited areas.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HVR2-G sequencing can be used to enhance molecular epidemiology surveillance of HRSV, particularly in areas where WGS may not be feasible. This integration allows for the use of historical data in conjunction with modern sequencing techniques.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not address potential limitations in the generalizability of the HVR2-G sequencing window to other regions or populations. The evidence is moderate as it is based on analysis of existing sequence data rather than new experimental findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the applicability of the HVR2-G sequencing window for lineage classification of human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) and its integration with the new WGS-defined lineage nomenclature. The research highlights that the HVR2-G region can reliably classify major HRSV lineages with a bootstrap over 70%, but nested lineages remain indistinguishable. Previous HVR2-G genotypes of HRSVA and B were reduced to fewer lineages using P-distance thresholds. The study suggests that HVR2-G sequencing can complement WGS in molecular virological surveillance, especially in resource-limited settings. However, the evidence is moderate as it relies on existing sequence data rather than new experimental findings, and the generalizability of the results to other populations is not addressed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 HVR2-G 测序窗口对于谱系分类的适用性,并将以前的 HVR2-G 基因型与新的 WGS 定义的谱系命名法相整合。人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (HRSV) 是引起婴儿、幼儿和老年人急性下呼吸道感染的主要病原体。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是使用 GenBank 的全 基因组 序列 (WGS) 数据和 Nextstrain 的谱系命名数据进行的。从这些序列中提取 HVR2-G 区域以评估其在谱系分类中的效用。
elements_zh.methods: HVR2-G 区域从 GenBank 的 WGS 序列中提取,谱系命名数据从 Nextstrain 下载。分别使用 IQ-TREE 2.3.6 和 MEGA11.0 进行 HVR2-G 序列的系统发育和核苷酸成对距离(p 距离)分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析表明,WGS定义的谱系命名法定义的主要谱系可以使用HVR2-G区域进行分类,自举率超过70%;无法区分嵌套的谱系。HRSVA 和 B 的 19 个和 37 个先前 HVR2-G 基因型分别减少为 4 个(A.1、A.2、A.3 和 A.D)和 5 个(B.1、B.2、B.3、B.4 和 B.D)谱系,P 距离阈值分别大于 0.102 和 0.0591。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究证实,HVR2-G 测序窗口提供了主要 HRSV 谱系的可靠分配,并能够与历史 监测 数据集集成。该方法有可能成为中国和全球HRSV分子病毒学监测全基因组测序(WGS)应用的补充,特别是在资源有限的地区。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,HVR2-G 测序可用于增强 HRSV 的分子 流行病学 监测,特别是在 WGS 可能不可行的领域。这种集成允许将历史数据与现代测序技术结合使用。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the applicability of the HVR2-G sequencing window for lineage classification and integrate previous HVR2-G genotypes with the new WGS-defined lineage nomenclature. Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) is a major pathogen causing acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children and older adults.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using whole-genome sequence (WGS) data from GenBank and lineage nomenclature data from Nextstrain. The HVR2-G region was extracted from these sequences to assess its utility in lineage classification.
analysis_en.methods: The HVR2-G region was extracted from WGS sequences from GenBank and the lineage nomenclature data were downloaded from Nextstrain. Phylogenetic and nucleotide pairwise distance (p-distance) analyses of HVR2-G sequences were conducted using IQ-TREE 2.3.6 and MEGA11.0, respectively.
analysis_en.main_results: Phylogenetic analyses revealed that the primary lineages defined by WGS-defined lineage nomenclature could be classified using the HVR2-G region with a bootstrap over 70%; the nested lineages could not be distinguished. Nineteen and 37 previous HVR2-G genotypes of HRSVA and B were reduced to 4 (A.1, A.2, A.3 and A.D) and 5 (B.1, B.2, B.3, B.4 and B.D) lineages with P-distance thresholds greater than 0.102 and 0.0591, respectively.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study confirmed that the HVR2-G sequencing window provides reliable assignment of major HRSV lineages and enables integration with historical surveillance datasets. This approach has the potential to serve as a complement to the application of WGS for molecular virological surveillance of HRSV in China and globally, especially in resource-limited areas.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HVR2-G sequencing can be used to enhance molecular epidemiology surveillance of HRSV, particularly in areas where WGS may not be feasible. This integration allows for the use of historical data in conjunction with modern sequencing techniques.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not address potential limitations in the generalizability of the HVR2-G sequencing window to other regions or populations. The evidence is moderate as it is based on analysis of existing sequence data rather than new experimental findings.

title: A digitalized nosocomial risk management framework during the COVID-19 pandemic: practice-based insights from a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China

source_records.title: A digitalized nosocomial risk management framework during the COVID-19 pandemic: practice-based insights from a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China

priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
full_text: BackgroundCancer patients represent a particularly vulnerable population during infectious disease outbreaks, with substantially elevated risk of infection and mortality compared to the general population. Comprehensive nosocomial risk management frameworks for specialized oncology hospitals remain under-documented in the literature.MethodsThis community case study describes a comprehensive, multi-component epidemic risk management program implemented at Sichuan Cancer Hospital—the largest tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China—from January 2020 to September 2022. The program integrated seven management pillars with a digital risk-reporting pipeline built on Questionnaire Star® and R programming language.ResultsOver the 32-month study period, the hospital achieved a 98% staff vaccination rate with 95% booster coverage. Following its deployment in August 2022, during the final weeks of the study period, the digital reporting system processed risk-investigation data and generated actionable summary tables within 5 min of submission. No nosocomial COVID-19 cases were detected among patients or staff during the surveillance period.ConclusionThe experience demonstrates that systematic integration of management innovations with digital technologies can support hospital infection prevention even under extreme epidemiological pressure; the absence of detected nosocomial cases, however, cannot be causally attributed to the program alone given concurrent community-level restrictions. The framework’s pathogen-agnostic architecture supports transferability to future respiratory virus epidemics in cancer hospital settings. 7Acknowledgment of conceptual and methodological constraintsThis study is subject to the following conceptual and methodological constraints: (1) the single-center design limits generalizability; findings should be validated in multi-center studies across diverse institutional and regulatory contexts. (2) The observational nature precludes causal attribution of the absence of detected nosocomial cases to specific program components. (3) The Zero-COVID policy period during which the program operated confounds the estimation of standalone program effectiveness. (4) Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections may have been undetected due to the absence of systematic asymptomatic screening. (5) The 32-month observation window does not capture the complete post-pandemic transition, and longer-term sustainability assessments are needed. (6) The digital pipeline’s performance was evaluated during a single hospital’s operations; scalability to multi-hospital networks remains untested. (7) Because systematic asymptomatic screening was not performed throughout the study period, the reported outcome refers to detected cases only. 5DiscussionThis community case study describes a comprehensive nosocomial epidemic risk management program implemented at a large tertiary cancer hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, yielding three principal findings: (1) the systematic integration of management innovations with digital technologies can function as a force multiplier for infection prevention; (2) the framework’s core architecture is pathogen-agnostic and transferable to future epidemic scenarios; and (3) no nosocomial COVID-19 cases were detected over 32 months despite repeated community outbreaks, a finding best interpreted as an association between the program and the absence of detected cases rather than proof of causation.5.1Integration of management and technology as a force multiplierThe program’s key innovation lies not in any single component but in the systematic integration of management strategies with digital technologies. The seven management pillars—leadership accountability, zoned-tiered prevention, epidemiological intelligence, grid-based supervision, network-based training, vaccination campaigns, and the digital pipeline (Table 1)—are individually well-documented in the infection prevention literature (11, 22–24), but their combined, mutually reinforcing implementation has not been described in a cancer hospital context. The digital pipeline in particular served as the informational backbone of the framework, enabling the rapid translation of raw risk-investigation data into actionable intelligence that directly informed management decisions. This finding aligns with recent systematic reviews showing that hospitals employing integrated, multi-component infection prevention bundles achieve superior outcomes compared to those implementing isolated interventions (24, 25). Layered multimodal quality-improvement initiatives have likewise demonstrated measurable reductions in device-associated infections in intensive care settings (26), further supporting the value of integrated rather than isolated interventions.5.2Transferability beyond COVID-19Although the program was developed and tested in the COVID-19 context, its core architecture is pathogen-agnostic. The structured data-capture templates in Questionnaire Star® can be rapidly reconfigured for other infectious disease threats (e.g., influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, or novel respiratory pathogens) by modifying the field set without altering the R processing logic. The R script’s modular design allows the addition of new data validation rules and the generation of pathogen-specific summary tables with minimal reprogramming. International equivalents of the data-capture platform [REDCap, Qualtrics, Google Forms (20)] and the platform-agnostic nature of the R back end (which accepts any structured CSV or Excel input) facilitate cross-border replication. This flexibility is particularly relevant given the increasing recognition that future respiratory virus epidemics are inevitable and that healthcare systems must maintain “warm” surveillance infrastructure between outbreaks (27, 28).5.3Comparison with published literatureThe existing literature on COVID-19 infection prevention and control in oncology settings can be broadly categorized into three groups: (a) clinical outcome studies reporting infection rates and mortality among cancer patients (5–9, 29); (b) expert commentaries and guideline documents providing management recommendations (10, 30–33); and (c) technology-focused reports on specific tools such as telehealth or health informatics systems (11, 14, 15). The present study contributes to a fourth, under-represented category: structured, practice-based descriptions of integrated frameworks that combine organizational and technological components into a coherent whole. Recent publications have emphasized the importance of such integrated approaches for post-pandemic preparedness (25–27), but detailed implementation accounts from specialized cancer hospitals remain limited. The R-based automated processing pipeline described here extends the existing literature on digital surveillance tools (15, 16, 25) by demonstrating a low-cost, platform-agnostic solution that does not require proprietary hospital information system integration.5.4Practical challenges and recommendationsSeveral challenges encountered during program implementation warrant discussion. First, information interoperability between medical institutions remains a systemic barrier: different hospitals in the same region used incompatible reporting systems, preventing cross-institutional risk data sharing. This limitation could be addressed through the adoption of standardized data exchange formats (e.g., HL7 FHIR) at the policy level. Second, the reliance on Questionnaire Star® as a commercial platform introduces a vendor-dependency risk; the platform-agnostic design described in Section 3.2.1 provides a mitigation strategy. Third, the initial configuration of the 17-field form required multiple iterations to balance comprehensiveness with completion time—a consideration for institutions developing similar tools. Finally, staff compliance with daily risk-reporting was initially suboptimal and required targeted communication campaigns and integration of reporting status into departmental performance metrics.5.5LimitationsThis report has several limitations that should be acknowledged. First, as a single-center case study, the generalizability of the findings to other institutional contexts—particularly hospitals with different resource levels, regulatory environments, or patient populations—requires further validation through multi-center replication studies. Second, the program was implemented during China’s “Zero-COVID” policy period, which included community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) such as lockdowns, mass testing, and travel restrictions. The observed absence of detected nosocomial cases reflects the combined effect of the hospital’s internal program and external community-level NPIs; isolating the independent contribution of the hospital’s program is not possible from this observational data. Future studies conducted in settings without concurrent community-level restrictions would help estimate the program’s standalone effectiveness. Third, asymptomatic infections may have gone undetected, as routine asymptomatic screening of all staff and patients was not systematically performed during the entire study period. Fourth, the 32-month observation window, while capturing multiple epidemic waves, does not include the full post-pandemic transition period. Finally, this report is observational in nature and was not designed as a controlled intervention study with a comparator group.5.6Interaction with community-level Zero-COVID policyAn important interpretative consideration is the interaction between the hospital’s internal program and China’s national Zero-COVID policy, which was active during the entire study period. Community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs)—including city-wide lockdowns during the August 2022 Chengdu outbreak, universal masking mandates, mass PCR testing, and inter-city travel restrictions—undoubtedly reduced the baseline risk of SARS-CoV-2 introduction into the hospital. However, several observations are consistent with a contribution of the hospital’s internal program to the absence of detected nosocomial cases. First, the hospital continued to receive patients from across Sichuan and neighboring provinces throughout the study period, including from regions with active community transmission, because cancer treatment cannot be indefinitely deferred. Second, the August 2022 Chengdu outbreak occurred despite existing community-level NPIs, indicating that community measures alone could not completely eliminate importation risk. Third, the digital pipeline was activated specifically in response to the failure of manual reporting channels during this outbreak, and the rapid availability of risk-stratified data directly enabled the leadership group to implement targeted, rather than blanket, staff deployment decisions—suggesting that the program may have added value beyond what community measures alone could provide. A cautious interpretation is therefore that the absence of detected nosocomial cases represents the combined effect of community-level NPIs and the hospital’s internal framework, with each component addressing different points in the transmission chain.5.7Post-study implementation example: influenza preparedness (2023–2024)Following the lifting of Zero-COVID restrictions in December 2022, and outside the stated study window (January 2020–September 2022), the hospital repurposed the digital risk-reporting pipeline for the 2023–2024 influenza season. The Questionnaire Star® form was reconfigured within 48 h by replacing COVID-19-specific fields (health code status, nucleic acid test results) with influenza-specific fields (influenza vaccination status, antiviral prophylaxis, symptom checklist), while preserving the demographic and contact-tracing fields. The R script required modification to only the variable-labeling module (approximately 20 lines of code), with the core data-cleaning, deduplication, and summary-table-generation logic remaining unchanged. This post-study implementation example demonstrates the framework’s operational flexibility and illustrates the feasibility of adapting the pathogen-agnostic architecture described in Section 5.2 to a different respiratory pathogen. Because this period falls outside the stated study window and systematic outcome data were not collected, it is reported as an implementation example rather than as a formal validation of the framework. 6ConclusionThis community case study demonstrates that a systematic, multi-component epidemic risk management program—integrating organizational strategies with a digital surveillance pipeline—was associated with an absence of detected nosocomial COVID-19 cases in a large tertiary cancer hospital, even under extreme epidemiological pressure. The framework’s pathogen-agnostic architecture, platform-agnostic data-processing logic, and modular R-based automation pipeline provide a replicable template for cancer hospitals and other specialized healthcare facilities preparing for future respiratory virus epidemics. While the absence of detected nosocomial cases must be interpreted in the context of concurrent community-level interventions during China’s Zero-COVID period, the program’s operational performance—particularly the <5-min data-processing capability and the successful repurposing for influenza surveillance—supports its practical utility. Multi-center replication studies in diverse regulatory and resource settings are needed to evaluate generalizability and to isolate the program’s independent contribution to nosocomial infection prevention. 1IntroductionThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), was first identified in Wuhan, China, in December 2019 and rapidly evolved into a global public health crisis, with the World Health Organization declaring a pandemic on March 11, 2020 (1, 2). The high transmissibility of SARS-CoV-2, with reproduction numbers varying across countries and prevention scenarios (3), and the clinical severity documented among early hospitalized cohorts (4), underscored the urgency of robust infection prevention. As of early 2023, COVID-19 had caused over 760 million confirmed cases and 6.9 million deaths worldwide.Cancer patients constitute a particularly high-risk group in the context of COVID-19. Immunosuppression resulting from both the malignancy itself and anticancer treatments (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy) elevates susceptibility to infection, while frequent hospital visits for treatment create repeated exposure opportunities. Studies have consistently reported that cancer patients with COVID-19 experience higher rates of severe illness, intensive care unit admission, and mortality compared to the general population (5–9).Despite the extensive literature on COVID-19 clinical outcomes in cancer patients, structured descriptions of comprehensive risk management frameworks implemented in oncology hospitals remain scarce. Most published reports focus on isolated interventions—such as triage protocols (10, 11), vaccination campaigns (12, 13), or telehealth adoption (14)—rather than integrated, multi-component programs. Furthermore, the role of digital tools in automating risk-investigation workflows within cancer hospitals has received limited attention (15–17).This community case study presents the design, implementation, and outcomes of a comprehensive epidemic risk management program at Sichuan Cancer Hospital, the largest specialized oncology center in Southwest China. Comprehensive nosocomial risk management frameworks for specialized oncology hospitals remain under-documented in the literature.MethodsThis community case study describes a comprehensive, multi-component epidemic risk management program implemented at Sichuan Cancer Hospital—the largest tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China—from January 2020 to September 2022. Following its deployment in August 2022, during the final weeks of the study period, the digital reporting system processed risk-investigation data and generated actionable summary tables within 5 min of submission. The framework’s pathogen-agnostic architecture supports transferability to future respiratory virus epidemics in cancer hospital settings.

(2) The observational nature precludes causal attribution of the absence of detected nosocomial cases to specific program components. (3) The Zero-COVID policy period during which the program operated confounds the estimation of standalone program effectiveness. (4) Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections may have been undetected due to the absence of systematic asymptomatic screening. (5) The 32-month observation window does not capture the complete post-pandemic transition, and longer-term sustainability assessments are needed. full_text_sections.discussion: 5DiscussionThis community case study describes a comprehensive nosocomial epidemic risk management program implemented at a large tertiary cancer hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, yielding three principal findings: (1) the systematic integration of management innovations with digital technologies can function as a force multiplier for infection prevention; (2) the framework’s core architecture is pathogen-agnostic and transferable to future epidemic scenarios; and (3) no nosocomial COVID-19 cases were detected over 32 months despite repeated community outbreaks, a finding best interpreted as an association between the program and the absence of detected cases rather than proof of causation.5.1Integration of management and technology as a force multiplierThe program’s key innovation lies not in any single component but in the systematic integration of management strategies with digital technologies. The seven management pillars—leadership accountability, zoned-tiered prevention, epidemiological intelligence, grid-based supervision, network-based training, vaccination campaigns, and the digital pipeline (Table 1)—are individually well-documented in the infection prevention literature (11, 22–24), but their combined, mutually reinforcing implementation has not been described in a cancer hospital context. The digital pipeline in particular served as the informational backbone of the framework, enabling the rapid translation of raw risk-investigation data into actionable intelligence that directly informed management decisions. This finding aligns with recent systematic reviews showing that hospitals employing integrated, multi-component infection prevention bundles achieve superior outcomes compared to those implementing isolated interventions (24, 25). Layered multimodal quality-improvement initiatives have likewise demonstrated measurable reductions in device-associated infections in intensive care settings (26), further supporting the value of integrated rather than isolated interventions.5.2Transferability beyond COVID-19Although the program was developed and tested in the COVID-19 context, its core architecture is pathogen-agnostic. The structured data-capture templates in Questionnaire Star® can be rapidly reconfigured for other infectious disease threats (e.g., influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, or novel respiratory pathogens) by modifying the field set without altering the R processing logic. The R script’s modular design allows the addition of new data validation rules and the generation of pathogen-specific summary tables with minimal reprogramming. International equivalents of the data-capture platform [REDCap, Qualtrics, Google Forms (20)] and the platform-agnostic nature of the R back end (which accepts any structured CSV or Excel input) facilitate cross-border replication. This flexibility is particularly relevant given the increasing recognition that future respiratory virus epidemics are inevitable and that healthcare systems must maintain “warm” surveillance infrastructure between outbreaks (27, 28).5.3Comparison with published literatureThe existing literature on COVID-19 infection prevention and control in oncology settings can be broadly categorized into three groups: (a) clinical outcome studies reporting infection rates and mortality among cancer patients (5–9, 29); (b) expert commentaries and guideline documents providing management recommendations (10, 30–33); and (c) technology-focused reports on specific tools such as telehealth or health informatics systems (11, 14, 15). The present study contributes to a fourth, under-represented category: structured, practice-based descriptions of integrated frameworks that combine organizational and technological components into a coherent whole. Recent publications have emphasized the importance of such integrated approaches for post-pandemic preparedness (25–27), but detailed implementation accounts from specialized cancer hospitals remain limited. The R-based automated processing pipeline described here extends the existing literature on digital surveillance tools (15, 16, 25) by demonstrating a low-cost, platform-agnostic solution that does not require proprietary hospital information system integration.5.4Practical challenges and recommendationsSeveral challenges encountered during program implementation warrant discussion. First, information interoperability between medical institutions remains a systemic barrier: different hospitals in the same region used incompatible reporting systems, preventing cross-institutional risk data sharing. This limitation could be addressed through the adoption of standardized data exchange formats (e.g., HL7 FHIR) at the policy level. Second, the reliance on Questionnaire Star® as a commercial platform introduces a vendor-dependency risk; the platform-agnostic design described in Section 3.2.1 provides a mitigation strategy. Third, the initial configuration of the 17-field form required multiple iterations to balance comprehensiveness with completion time—a consideration for institutions developing similar tools. Finally, staff compliance with daily risk-reporting was initially suboptimal and required targeted communication campaigns and integration of reporting status into departmental performance metrics.5.5LimitationsThis report has several limitations that should be acknowledged. First, as a single-center case study, the generalizability of the findings to other institutional contexts—particularly hospitals with different resource levels, regulatory environments, or patient populations—requires further validation through multi-center replication studies. Second, the program was implemented during China’s “Zero-COVID” policy period, which included community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) such as lockdowns, mass testing, and travel restrictions. The observed absence of detected nosocomial cases reflects the combined effect of the hospital’s internal program and external community-level NPIs; isolating the independent contribution of the hospital’s program is not possible from this observational data. Future studies conducted in settings without concurrent community-level restrictions would help estimate the program’s standalone effectiveness. Third, asymptomatic infections may have gone undetected, as routine asymptomatic screening of all staff and patients was not systematically performed during the entire study period. Fourth, the 32-month observation window, while capturing multiple epidemic waves, does not include the full post-pandemic transition period. Finally, this report is observational in nature and was not designed as a controlled intervention study with a comparator group.5.6Interaction with community-level Zero-COVID policyAn important interpretative consideration is the interaction between the hospital’s internal program and China’s national Zero-COVID policy, which was active during the entire study period. Community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs)—including city-wide lockdowns during the August 2022 Chengdu outbreak, universal masking mandates, mass PCR testing, and inter-city travel restrictions—undoubtedly reduced the baseline risk of SARS-CoV-2 introduction into the hospital. However, several observations are consistent with a contribution of the hospital’s internal program to the absence of detected nosocomial cases. First, the hospital continued to receive patients from across Sichuan and neighboring provinces throughout the study period, including from regions with active community transmission, because cancer treatment cannot be indefinitely deferred. Second, the August 2022 Chengdu outbreak occurred despite existing community-level NPIs, indicating that community measures alone could not completely eliminate importation risk. full_text_sections.conclusion: 6ConclusionThis community case study demonstrates that a systematic, multi-component epidemic risk management program—integrating organizational strategies with a digital surveillance pipeline—was associated with an absence of detected nosocomial COVID-19 cases in a large tertiary cancer hospital, even under extreme epidemiological pressure. The framework’s pathogen-agnostic architecture, platform-agnostic data-processing logic, and modular R-based automation pipeline provide a replicable template for cancer hospitals and other specialized healthcare facilities preparing for future respiratory virus epidemics. While the absence of detected nosocomial cases must be interpreted in the context of concurrent community-level interventions during China’s Zero-COVID period, the program’s operational performance—particularly the <5-min data-processing capability and the successful repurposing for influenza surveillance—supports its practical utility. Multi-center replication studies in diverse regulatory and resource settings are needed to evaluate generalizability and to isolate the program’s independent contribution to nosocomial infection prevention.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), was first identified in Wuhan, China, in December 2019 and rapidly evolved into a global public health crisis, with the World Health Organization declaring a pandemic on March 11, 2020 (1, 2). As of early 2023, COVID-19 had caused over 760 million confirmed cases and 6.9 million deaths worldwide.Cancer patients constitute a particularly high-risk group in the context of COVID-19. Immunosuppression resulting from both the malignancy itself and anticancer treatments (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy) elevates susceptibility to infection, while frequent hospital visits for treatment create repeated exposure opportunities. Studies have consistently reported that cancer patients with COVID-19 experience higher rates of severe illness, intensive care unit admission, and mortality compared to the general population (5–9).Despite the extensive literature on COVID-19 clinical outcomes in cancer patients, structured descriptions of comprehensive risk management frameworks implemented in oncology hospitals remain scarce. Most published reports focus on isolated interventions—such as triage protocols (10, 11), vaccination campaigns (12, 13), or telehealth adoption (14)—rather than integrated, multi-component programs. Furthermore, the role of digital tools in automating risk-investigation workflows within cancer hospitals has received limited attention (15–17).This community case study presents the design, implementation, and outcomes of a comprehensive epidemic risk management program at Sichuan Cancer Hospital, the largest specialized oncology center in Southwest China. title_original: A digitalized nosocomial risk management framework during the COVID-19 pandemic: practice-based insights from a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digitalized nosocomial risk management framework in preventing SARS-CoV-2 transmission within a tertiary cancer hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, given the heightened vulnerability of cancer patients to infection and mortality.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a single-center case study conducted at a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China over a 32-month period, focusing on the implementation of a digitalized risk management program during the national Zero-COVID policy period.
analysis.methods: The program utilized a digital risk-reporting pipeline built on Questionnaire Star® and R programming language, incorporating systematic integration of management strategies with digital technologies, and relied on community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) such as lockdowns, mass testing, and travel restrictions.
analysis.main_results: Over the 32-month study period, the hospital achieved a 98% staff vaccination rate with 95% booster coverage. No nosocomial COVID-19 cases were detected among patients or staff during the surveillance period. The program was reconfigured within 48 hours to address other infectious diseases such as influenza.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the absence of detected nosocomial cases as an association rather than proof of causation, noting that the program's effectiveness may have been influenced by concurrent community-level restrictions. The novelty lies in demonstrating the utility of integrated, multi-component infection prevention strategies using digital tools.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that systematic integration of management innovations with digital technologies can support hospital infection prevention during outbreaks, particularly in high-risk settings like cancer hospitals, and highlight the importance of such frameworks for post-pandemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design, which restricts generalizability, and the concurrent community-level restrictions that may have confounded the assessment of the program's standalone effectiveness. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates a digitalized nosocomial risk management framework implemented at a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China during the COVID-19 pandemic. The framework integrated management strategies with digital technologies, including a Questionnaire Star®-based surveillance system and R programming language. Over 32 months, the hospital achieved a high staff vaccination rate and did not detect any nosocomial COVID-19 cases, despite repeated community outbreaks. The authors interpret these results as an association rather than proof of causation, given the concurrent national Zero-COVID policy. The study highlights the potential of integrated, multi-component infection prevention strategies for high-risk settings and post-pandemic preparedness. However, its single-center design limits generalizability, and further multi-center studies are needed to validate the framework's effectiveness. The findings suggest that digital tools can support hospital infection prevention, but their standalone impact remains unclear due to overlapping public health measures.

abstract_zh: 文献中对肿瘤专科医院的综合院内风险管理框架的记录仍然不足。方法本社区案例研究描述了中国西南最大的三级肿瘤医院四川省肿瘤医院(中国西南最大的三级癌症医院)从 2020 年 1 月至 2022 年 9 月实施的一项全面的、多组成部分的流行病风险管理项目。该项目将七个管理支柱与基于 Questionnaire Star® 和 R 编程语言构建的数字风险报告管道集成在一起。结果在 32 个月的研究期间,该医院实现了 98% 的员工 疫苗接种 率和 95% 的助推器覆盖率。继 2022 年 8 月部署后,在研究期的最后几周,数字报告系统处理了风险调查数据,并在提交后 5 分钟内生成了可操作的汇总表。7 承认概念和方法上的限制本研究受到以下概念和方法上的限制:(1)单中心设计限制了普遍性;研究结果应在不同机构和监管背景下的多中心研究中得到验证。(7)由于整个研究期间没有进行系统的无症状筛查,因此报告的结果仅指发现的病例。背景癌症患者是传染病 暴发 期间特别脆弱的人群,与一般人群相比,感染和 暴发 的风险显着升高。监测期间,患者或工作人员中没有发现院内COVID-19病例。结论经验表明,即使在极端的流行病学压力下,管理创新与数字技术的系统整合也可以支持医院感染预防。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估在 COVID-19 大流行期间,数字化医院风险管理框架在三级癌症医院内预防 SARS-CoV-2 传播 的有效性,因为癌症患者对感染和 死亡率 的脆弱性更高。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在中国西南地区一家三级肿瘤医院进行的为期 32 个月的单中心案例研究,重点关注国家“零新冠”政策期间数字化风险管理计划的实施情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 该计划利用基于 Questionnaire Star® 和 R 编程语言构建的数字风险报告管道,将管理策略与数字技术系统集成,并依靠社区层面的非药物干预措施 (NPI),例如封锁、大规模检测和旅行限制。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 32 个月的研究期间,医院实现了 98% 的员工 疫苗接种 率和 95% 的加强覆盖率。监测 期间,在患者或工作人员中未发现院内 COVID-19 病例。该计划在 48 小时内进行了重新配置,以应对流感等其他传染病。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将未发现院内病例解释为一种关联,而不是因果关系的证据,并指出该计划的有效性可能受到同时存在的社区层面限制的影响。新颖之处在于使用数字工具展示集成的、多成分的感染预防策略的实用性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,管理创新与数字技术的系统整合可以支持 暴发 期间的医院感染预防,特别是在癌症医院等高风险环境中,并强调了此类框架对于大流行后准备的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到单中心设计的限制,限制了普遍性,并且同时存在的社区层面的限制可能会混淆对该项目独立有效性的评估。由于这些限制,证据是中等的。
